topic: Retry on throttling
detail: Violated: Treat 429 (throttling) and transient network errors as transient: honor Retry‑After / retry-after-ms headers and retry with exponential backoff and jitter to avoid throttling loops. Evidence: No retry/backoff implementation present in code; MongoClient calls are direct (aml_agent/analysis.py, seed.py).
proposed_change: Add a retry wrapper for DB calls that honors Retry-After and implements exponential backoff with jitter.

topic: Avoid synchronous long-running analysis
detail: Violated: Avoid running long-running synchronous analysis inside request/response handlers; run heavy aggregations or graph jobs as background tasks or batch jobs and return job IDs for async processing. Evidence: FastAPI endpoint calls analyze() synchronously (app/main.py:11-16) which performs aggregations inline (aml_agent/analysis.py).
proposed_change: Run analysis as a background task (FastAPI BackgroundTasks, Celery, or return a job id and process offline) and provide a status/result endpoint.

topic: Bulk load best practice
detail: Violated: When bulk-loading, use bulk_write / bulk insert with appropriate batch sizes and unordered mode, and create indexes after the bulk load when possible to speed ingestion. Evidence: seed.py creates indexes before bulk_write (seed.py lines 18-23, then performs bulk writes at lines 38-39 and 87-88).
proposed_change: Move index creation until after bulk_write or use background:true index creation; use unordered bulk writes and batch sizes appropriate for the cluster.

topic: PII redaction
detail: Violated: Detect/redact or pseudonymize PII before sending data to external LLM/embedding services and use Azure PII-detection/redaction features or enterprise Azure OpenAI privacy controls when possible. Evidence: llm.py builds prompts including raw details and passes them to LLM without redaction (aml_agent/llm.py lines 21-25). summarize_flags will pass account IDs to llm_client (aml_agent/analysis.py lines 96-105).
proposed_change: Add PII-detection/redaction step before constructing prompts (or provide an option to pseudonymize account IDs and redact sensitive fields).

topic: Mask logs
detail: Violated: Mask or redact sensitive fields in application logs and exported narratives (e.g., partially mask account IDs) and enforce role-based access to investigative artifacts. Evidence: summarize_flags returns narratives containing raw account/tx ids (aml_agent/analysis.py lines 100-106) and logs/prints (run.py prints results lines 16-19) without redaction.
proposed_change: Implement redaction/masking in summarize_flags and any logging output (e.g., show only last 4 characters of account ids).

topic: Schema versioning
detail: Violated: Add a schemaVersion field to documents and migrate lazily so analysis and migration code can evolve safely. Evidence: seed.py account and transaction documents have no schemaVersion field (seed.py lines 27-36 and 48-85).
proposed_change: Add schemaVersion when inserting documents and add a short doc in README about migration strategy.

topic: Client-side rate limiting
detail: Violated: Implement client-side rate limiting and batching when performing many lookups or embedding requests to avoid bursts that trigger throttling or RU spikes. Evidence: No client-side rate limiting or batching logic for lookups/embeddings in code (analysis/llm/seed are direct calls).
proposed_change: Add a simple rate-limiter for embedding calls and bulk DB lookups, or batch requests with small delays and exponential backoff.

topic: Exact vector index creation syntax
detail: Missing: A verified, copy-pasteable create_index example for Azure DocumentDB's vector indexes (the exact option names such as vectorOptions/indexOptions, algorithm names, and where to supply dims and distance). Looked in: No documentation server available during this run (documentation_search_available=false); I inspected local files (seed_data.py, README.md) which contain best-effort placeholders but not authoritative syntax. Effect: The seed script used a plausible create_index and caught failures; without exact syntax the sample cannot demonstrate a tested server-side vector index creation, and end users will need to verify and update the index code for their cluster.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short page in the agent-kit or README titled 'Creating a vector index on Azure DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible)'. Include: (1) the tested createIndex call (code snippet) that works against the managed cluster, (2) example values for algorithm (ivf/hnsw/diskann), dims (match embedding model), and distance (cosine), (3) example error messages and how to fall back to client-side, (4) a minimal shell and Python/pymongo example. Mark as high priority.

topic: Vector-search aggregation/operator names
detail: Missing: The exact aggregation stage/operator ($search/$vectorSearch/knnBeta or provider-specific name) and the meta-score key names used to project similarity scores from server-side vector search. Looked in: No external docs available; local code contains placeholders (src/agent.py uses an addFields + $meta placeholder). Effect: The implementation falls back to client-side similarity because the operator names and syntax were not verified. Without the operator names the sample cannot demonstrate server-side KNN search semantics or return official server-side similarity scores.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short example in the README or an agent-kit page titled 'Running vector KNN queries' that shows the working aggregation pipeline for the managed cluster, including how to pass the query vector, how to request the top-k, how to project the provider's search score (e.g., $meta: 'searchScore'), and how to interpret returned fields. Include language and Python/pymongo examples, plus fallback recipes.

topic: Embedding provider & embedding dimensions
detail: Missing: Authoritative guidance on which embedding provider(s) the sample should support, the env var names for provider credentials, and how to determine/check the model output dimensionality so indices and stored vectors match the chosen model. Looked in: Local repo (.env.example, agent.py, seed_data.py) and readiness notes; no external docs reachable in this run. Effect: The demo uses mock 128-d embeddings; when switching to a real provider (e.g., OpenAI) real embeddings may have a different dimension (e.g., 1536), which would require re-seeding and index recreation. This mismatch was flagged in the readiness report and partially implemented (seed remains deterministic).
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] Add an agent-kit rule and README section 'Embedding provider selection' that: (1) lists supported providers (OpenAI, etc.), (2) declares the env var names (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY), (3) shows how to query or assert the embedding dimension and set EMBED_DIM via env var or model metadata, (4) instructs to re-seed stored vectors when switching providers, and (5) includes a short Python snippet to validate stored vectors' length against the model output at startup.

topic: Index tuning parameters for sample size
detail: Missing: Practical guidance and example parameter values (nlist, probes, efConstruction, M, etc.) appropriate for small demo datasets vs. production-scale collections. proposed_change: [learn_doc] A 'Vector index tuning' page showing recommended defaults for demo (<10k vectors), medium (10k–1M), and large (>1M) datasets; provide sample create_index parameter sets for IVF and HNSW, guidance on measuring recall/throughput, and commands to rebuild indexes. Include examples and recommended monitoring metrics.

topic: Avoid fetching all embeddings

topic: Bulk seed writes

proposed_change: Switch to bulk_write with ordered operations for initial load, add rate limiting and exponential backoff on 429, and document recommended RU provisioning for bulk ingestion.

topic: Embedding storage type and indexing
detail: Missing: A short, prominent statement in the vector-search docs and sample quickstarts that explicitly says: 'Vectors must be stored as number[] (an array of numbers) to be indexed by cosmosSearch; packing embeddings into BSON Binary will not be indexed.' The repository README mentions packed-Binary but does not make this caution prominent. Looked in: documentdb-vector-search skill, 'Integrated vector store' Microsoft docs, sample README and code; discover step found the number[] requirement but the sample still stored Binary. Effect: The builder followed the prompt and stored binary-packed embeddings; as a result server-side vector indexing will likely not work and the sample falls back to in-memory ranking. This reduces the sample's value as a demonstration of server-side vector-ivf search.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Add a short 'Indexable vector storage' note to the top of the 'Vector search' documentation and to the sample README. Example text: 'Important: To be indexed by DocumentDB's cosmosSearch vector indexes, store vectors as an array of numbers (e.g., embedding: [0.123, ...]). Storing embeddings as BSON Binary (packed float32) is compact but will not be indexed. If you must store Binary for offline use, also persist a number[] copy or use a separate index pipeline.'

topic: IVF numLists sizing
detail: Violated: When using IVF, choose numLists relative to dataset size (use documentCount/1000 for up to ~1M documents, and consider other index types like DiskANN beyond that); tune nProbes to trade recall for latency. Evidence: app/scripts/create_vector_index.py:27-31 (cosmosSearchOptions.options: {'nlist': 100}) — nlist=100 is not tuned relative to dataset size (demo has 5 documents).
proposed_change: Set a conservative demo default (e.g., nlist = min(32, max(1, document_count//1000))) or compute nlist from collection count; document the heuristic in the index script.

topic: Embedding storage type
detail: Violated: Store vectors as numeric arrays (number[]) so they can be indexed; embedding values stored as other types (for example raw BSON Binary) are not accepted by the vector index and will not be indexed. Evidence: app/scripts/load_data.py:79-83 (packs normalized float32 into Binary and sets doc['embedding'] = Binary(packed)); app/app.py uses Binary in searches (pack_embedding/unpack functions).
proposed_change: Store embeddings as a numeric array: doc['embedding'] = vec.tolist() (float32), and update create_vector_index/aggregation usage accordingly. Update README to warn builders that Binary-packed embeddings will not be indexed by cosmosSearch.

topic: Prefer Entra ID for auth
detail: Violated: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC) + role-based access control for cluster authentication and management rather than embedding long-lived cluster passwords in code; Entra ID can be enabled as an auth mode on the cluster and you can register service principals or managed identities. Evidence: The sample uses MONGO_URI connection strings and .env.example; README does not document Entra ID usage or why it is not used in the demo.
proposed_change: Add a README section showing how to use Microsoft Entra ID (example with azure-identity and PyMongo MONGODB-OIDC) or state clearly why the sample uses connection-string auth for the quickstart.

topic: Retries & 429 handling
detail: Violated: Handle transient errors and rate limits with retries and exponential backoff, and treat HTTP 429 / rate-limiting specially (respect any Retry-After header and instrument throttling metrics). Evidence: app/app.py and scripts/load_data.py do not implement retries or exponential backoff around MongoClient operations or embedding API calls; the code catches exceptions but does not retry.
proposed_change: Add retry wrappers with exponential backoff (respect Retry-After for 429s) around db.command, coll.aggregate and OpenAI calls; consider using tenacity or similar retry libs.

topic: Verify index availability
detail: Violated: Verify index creation and availability before sending search traffic (make index creation idempotent and check listIndexes/getIndexes or createIndexes response). Evidence: app/scripts/create_vector_index.py prints the payload and attempts db.command but there is no code that verifies the index exists before the Flask app starts or prevents searches while index build/incompatibility exists. app/app.py relies on catching exceptions at query time and falling back to in-memory ranking (app/app.py:101-121, 122-146).
proposed_change: Modify create_vector_index.py to check getIndexes/listIndexes and block/return error until index is 'ready', or add an app startup check that refuses $search until index is present. Persist the admin payload if the gateway rejects the command.

topic: Binary artifacts & indexing
detail: Violated: If you choose to store embedding-related binary artifacts for non-index use (for example compact on-disk storage), document the serialization format and be aware that the DocumentDB vector index requires number[] for indexing so binary blobs won't be queryable by cosmosSearch. Evidence: app/scripts/load_data.py writes Binary(packed float32) (line 81). README.md:46 documents packing as 'BSON Binary (packed float32 little-endian)' but does not clearly say this will not be indexed by cosmosSearch.
proposed_change: Either store as number[] so server-side indexing works, or (if Binary is required) explicitly document the choice and note that such Binary embeddings will not be indexed by cosmosSearch (and give the alternative indexing approach).

detail: Violated: Honor throttling signals (HTTP 429) from Azure services: respect Retry-After headers when present and otherwise use bounded exponential backoff with jitter; use circuit breakers and avoid retry storms/enqueuing retries that block threads. topic: Use projection
detail: Violated: Use projection to return only the fields required by the application to reduce network payloads and throughput/cost (return stored source or selected fields only). proposed_change: Use projection in coll.find(filter_q, projection={...}) to return only the fields needed for ranking (e.g., trial_id, title, summary, criteria, embedding when needed).

topic: Idempotent writes & retries
detail: Violated: Design write operations to be idempotent (use upserts with a stable key where appropriate) and implement retries for transient failures with exponential backoff and jitter; ensure retries are safe for non-idempotent operations. Evidence: Seed upserts with update_one(..., upsert=True) (seed.py:75) but runtime match writes use insert_one without retries (app/app/main.py:183-191). No retry/backoff logic present in code.
proposed_change: Use upsert or a stable id for match writes and add a small retry decorator with exponential backoff for transient errors; document retry semantics and safe idempotence choices.

topic: JSON Schema validation
detail: Violated: Use JSON Schema validation ($jsonSchema) where supported to enforce collection-level schema constraints and catch malformed updates early. Evidence: No collection-level validator is created by seed.py; the seed only creates scalar indexes (seed.py:61-63).
proposed_change: Add a JSON Schema validator when creating the collection in seed.py (or via createCollection with validator) to assert required fields and types for trials.

proposed_change: Add a README section 'Observability' describing how to enable diagnostic settings and how to capture explain() plans (including an example explain call), and include a small helper script (optional) that runs explain() for representative queries.

detail: Missing: The sample opens a change stream but does not persist resume tokens or implement a restart/backoff policy; the quick verification timed out in this environment. Public docs explain resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime but the sample does not demonstrate checkpointing. Looked in: Inspected app/src/watch.js and scripts/watch_once.js; reviewed Microsoft Learn 'Change streams in Azure DocumentDB' and documentdb-change-streams guidance. Effect: Caused incomplete verification of end-to-end change-stream behavior in this run; a developer following the sample may run into missed events or inability to resume after process failure without extra code.
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] Add a short sample to src/watch.js (or src/watch_persistent.js) that writes the last resume token to a durable 'watch_checkpoints' collection after processing each change; on startup the watcher should read the last token and call coll.watch({ }, { resumeAfter: token }). Also provide a small README section explaining resumability, example token schema, and how to test locally (watch_once with token snapshot).

topic: Bulk-write partial-failure handling
detail: Missing: The ingest path does unordered bulk writes but does not inspect individual writeErrors to retry only retryable failures (it only logs the error). The public guidance recommends inspecting BulkWriteResult/writeErrors and not re-running whole batches. Looked in: Inspected app/src/ingest.js and searched Microsoft Learn bulk-write guidance and the documentdb-agent-kit for best-practice handling of bulk failures. Effect: Leaves production ingestion fragile: transient or rate-limit failures are not retried in an idempotent, selective way; duplicate-key errors are not explicitly counted or surfaced for monitoring.
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] Add a helper that, given a BulkWriteResult or MongoBulkWriteError, extracts writeErrors and partitions them into non-retryable (duplicate-key 11000) and retryable sets. Retry only the retryable operations with backoff; record metrics for duplicate-key counts. Provide example code and tests.

topic: Transactions for ingestion
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Avoid multi-document transactions for high-throughput ingestion; prefer single-document writes and idempotent design.
proposed_change: A public document that explicitly discusses transaction trade-offs for high-throughput ingestion in Azure DocumentDB would let agents evaluate this more confidently.

topic: Resume tokens
detail: Violated: Persist and periodically checkpoint change-stream resume tokens so a consumer can resume after crashes. Evidence: app/src/watch.js opens a change stream but does not persist resume tokens; changeStream.on('change', ...) does not checkpoint lastResumeToken. scripts/watch_once.js timed out during verification (events show a timeout), and watch.js exits on error (lines 29-32) rather than implementing durable resume logic.
proposed_change: Persist change.stream.resumeToken (or change._id) to a durable store (collection or external store) after successful processing; on restart use resumeAfter or startAtOperationTime. Add retry/backoff on transient errors.

topic: Change-stream options & resiliency
detail: Violated: Open change streams with appropriate pipeline/options and monitor resumability; implement backoff/retry on transient errors. Evidence: app/src/watch.js uses coll.watch([], { fullDocument: 'updateLookup' }) (line 13) but lacks resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime handling, no maxAwaitTimeMS, and the error handler exits the process (lines 29-32) instead of implementing exponential backoff and restart logic.
proposed_change: Implement a restart loop that records the last resume token, handles resumable vs non-resumable errors, uses exponential backoff with jitter on retry, and configures options like maxAwaitTimeMS and fullDocument per workload.

topic: Bulk failure handling
detail: Violated: Examine BulkWriteResult/writeErrors on partial bulk failures and retry only the failed operations that are retryable. Evidence: app/src/ingest.js calls bulkWrite and in its catch block logs the error (lines 40-42) but does not inspect err.writeErrors or retry retryable ops selectively.
proposed_change: On MongoBulkWriteError inspect err.writeErrors, filter out duplicate-key errors (11000) and only retry retryable errors; consider returning failed-op ids to a retry queue.

topic: Retries & backoff
detail: Violated: Normalize exponential backoff with jitter for retries and respect server retry-after headers for rate-limited responses. Evidence: ingest.flush() catch block logs errors but does not implement retry/backoff policy (app/src/ingest.js lines 40-42).
proposed_change: Implement idempotent retry mechanism with exponential backoff and jitter for retryable write failures; consider an outbox/queue for permanent retries.

topic: Use Entra ID when available
detail: Violated: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) + RBAC / managed identities for app authentication rather than long-lived DB passwords; create least-privilege secondary users if SCRAM is necessary. Evidence: app/README.md and app/app/db.py use DOCUMENTDB_URI and do not document or demonstrate Microsoft Entra ID flows or explain why Entra ID was not used (app/README.md lines 7-9, app/app/db.py:12-16).

topic: Explain queries
detail: Violated: Run explain()/explain('executionStats') on queries and aggregation pipelines to verify index usage and to tune pipelines. Evidence: No code calls explain() or uses MCP explain tools on the aggregation pipeline; scripts/aggregate_test.py runs the aggregation but does not call explain (app/scripts/aggregate_test.py:13-24).
proposed_change: Add an example script (or an extra CLI/seed step) that runs db.collection.explain('executionStats') on the aggregation pipeline and record the output. Or use the DocumentDB MCP tool (documentdb_explain) in the repo's verification scripts.

topic: Respect backpressure (429)
detail: Violated: On HTTP 429 read Retry-After and apply exponential backoff with jitter; enqueue retries rather than blocking and limit retry counts. Evidence: app/app/main.py and seed.py do not implement retry/backoff or inspect Retry-After; coll.insert_many() calls are not wrapped with retry logic.
proposed_change: Wrap insert_many and other bulk operations with a retry loop that honours Retry-After header when present and otherwise uses exponential backoff with jitter; prefer unordered writes and enqueue retries rather than blocking the API worker.

topic: Bulk/unordered writes
detail: Violated: For high-throughput ingestion use bulk/unordered writes and tune batch sizes (commonly up to ~1,000 documents per batch per process). Evidence: app/app/main.py uses coll.insert_many(docs) without ordered=False and without batching; app/seed.py uses insert_many for small lists but no ordered=False.
proposed_change: Use insert_many(docs, ordered=False) and implement configurable batching (e.g., chunk parsed_docs into batches of 500) to reduce tail latencies and allow partial success handling.

topic: Monetary amounts type
detail: Violated: Store monetary amounts using fixed-point or BSON Decimal128 rather than binary float to avoid precision errors when summing. Evidence: app/app/models.py:12 defines amount: Optional[float]; seed and parser produce float values (app/app/parser.py:42-45), and aggregation sums those floats (app/app/main.py:64-67).
proposed_change: Change model amount to use Decimal, map to BSON Decimal128 on insert (use bson.decimal128.Decimal128 or PyMongo's Decimal128 wrapper) and update parser to return Decimal; document the rationale in README.

topic: Daily-group key
detail: Violated: Keep a date-truncated field for daily aggregations so grouping is efficient and indexable. Evidence: app/app/main.py groups by a formatted value_date via $dateToString in aggregation but the stored documents do not include a truncated day field; create_indexes.py indexes (message_type, value_date) but not a truncated day field.
proposed_change: Compute and store a message_date_day (YYYY-MM-DD) at insert time (in seed.py and /ingest) and add a compound index on (message_type, message_date_day) to make daily grouping use the index.

topic: Operation timeouts
detail: Violated: Configure per-operation timeouts and serverSelection/socket timeouts to avoid indefinite hangs. Evidence: app/app/db.py creates AsyncIOMotorClient(uri) without explicit serverSelectionTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS (app/app/db.py:15).
proposed_change: Pass serverSelectionTimeoutMS (e.g., 5000) and socketTimeoutMS appropriate for bulk ops to AsyncIOMotorClient or add them to the connection URI; document recommended values in README.

topic: Observability

topic: Partial index for uncategorized
detail: Violated: Use partial indexes (partialFilterExpression) to index only the subset of documents your query filters on to reduce index size and write cost (e.g., index only documents where category does not exist). Evidence: app/scripts/seed.js line 9 creates index { date: 1, category: 1 } but no partial index on category:{ $exists:false } is created.
proposed_change: Create a partial index for categorization scans, e.g. coll.createIndex({ date:1, category:1 }, { partialFilterExpression: { category: { $exists: false } } }) in the seed script.

topic: Idempotent categorization updates
detail: Violated: Make categorization updates idempotent by using conditional updates (e.g. filter { _id:..., category: { $exists: false } } and $set the category), avoiding blind re-writes so multiple runs won't overwrite audited labels. Evidence: app/src/index.js lines 30-33 and app/scripts/run_categorization.js lines 11-14 call updateOne({ _id: doc._id }, { $set: { category } }) without a conditional filter to ensure category doesn't already exist. The code fetches only uncategorized docs in the query, but the update itself is blind and would overwrite if concurrency or race conditions occur.
proposed_change: Use a conditional update filter to make updates atomic and idempotent, e.g. coll.updateOne({ _id: doc._id, category: { $exists: false } }, { $set: { category } }).

proposed_change: If some collections may contain documents without transactionRef, create a partial index: TransactionSchema.index({ transactionRef:1 }, { unique:true, partialFilterExpression: { transactionRef: { $exists: true } } }); otherwise ensure transactionRef is required (it currently is) and document that invariant.

topic: Session + withTransaction pattern
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Use explicit client sessions and withTransaction to group multi-document operations, and pass the session to every operation in the transaction callback.
proposed_change: A short 'Transactions with Mongoose' snippet on the Mongoose + DocumentDB quickstart showing startSession(), session.withTransaction(callback, options) and the explicit passing of { session } to every Model operation.

topic: Monetary types
detail: Violated: Store monetary values using a precise numeric type (Decimal128) or integer minor-units (cents) rather than floating-point. Evidence: app/src/models/transaction.js (line 6 defines amount: { type: Number }) and app/src/models/account.js (line 6 balance: { type: Number }).
proposed_change: Change amount and account.balance to Decimal128 or use integer cents. Example: amount: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.Decimal128, required: true } and convert inputs via Decimal128.fromString() or store amounts in cents as integers.

topic: Retries policy
detail: Violated: Do not blindly retry whole transactions on any error; implement retries only for transient faults with exponential backoff and idempotent writes. Evidence: No driver-level retry logic or error-label handling in app/src/transactions.js; withTransaction is used but no explicit retry/backoff is implemented.
proposed_change: Add a bounded retry loop around session.withTransaction that retries only when errors are labeled TransientTransactionError or UnknownTransactionCommitResult, with exponential backoff and a small max attempt count.

topic: Numeric types in updates
detail: Violated: Use proper numeric types in queries and updates (Decimal128 or integer cents) and ensure the ODM casts values correctly when using atomic operators like $inc. Evidence: app/src/models/transaction.js (amount: Number, line 6) and app/src/models/account.js (balance: Number, line 6); $inc operations in app/src/transactions.js (line 26) operate on Number fields.
proposed_change: Migrate amount and balance to Decimal128 or store amounts in minor-units (integer cents); update code paths to convert inputs/outputs and ensure $inc uses Decimal128-aware increments.

topic: Monitoring and RU awareness
detail: Violated: Monitor request-unit (RU/s) consumption, index usage and throttling; alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/connection saturation. Evidence: No metrics or monitoring instrumentation in the sample (no telemetry or Azure Monitor wiring).
proposed_change: Add minimal instrumentation: counters for transaction commits/failures, duplicate-key events, retry counts; export via Prometheus client or Azure Monitor SDK and document configuration in README.

topic: Audit metadata
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Keep detailed immutable audit metadata on each Transaction (createdAt, createdBy, transactionRef...).
proposed_change: A short doc on the quickstart page listing recommended readonly audit fields for ledger transactions (createdAt, createdBy, transactionRef, source).

topic: TTL on ledger
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Avoid TTL indexes on immutable ledgers.
proposed_change: An explicit note on a DocumentDB data-modeling page that 'do not use TTL on ledger collections; if expiry is required put expirable docs in a separate collection' would help agent decisions.

topic: Operational metrics
detail: Violated: Instrument and emit operational metrics for transaction commit failures, retry counts, duplicate-key events, RU/throughput throttling, and slow queries. Evidence: No telemetry, metrics or logging for metrics events in repository.
proposed_change: Instrument counters and histograms (e.g., transaction_commits_total, transaction_commit_failures_total, duplicate_key_events_total) and export via Prometheus or Azure Monitor. Add examples in README for wiring.

proposed_change: Offload webhook delivery to a background worker or message queue; in the short term, perform non-blocking enqueue (e.g., write delivery requests to a 'deliveries' collection and process them with a separate worker) so the watch loop returns quickly.

topic: Compound index ESR
detail: Violated: Follow the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) when creating compound indexes for queries and aggregation match stages. Evidence: Alert-rule queries use userId + active + symbol semantics; existing indexes include userId and userId+active but not a full { userId:1, active:1, symbol:1 } compound index to cover the common predicate, so some queries may still require extra work. (app/src/models/alertrule.js shows defined indexes.)
proposed_change: Add a compound index on { userId: 1, active: 1, symbol: 1 } to avoid scans when matching rules by userId, active and symbol.

topic: allowDiskUse
detail: Violated: When running potentially large aggregations, enable allowDiskUse: true and minimize projection/result shape to reduce data transferred over the wire. Evidence: Aggregations in app/src/app.js and scripts/aggregate_test.js call Position.aggregate(...) but do not pass the option { allowDiskUse: true } for large workloads.
proposed_change: Pass { allowDiskUse: true } to aggregate when running larger datasets or document this option in README and conditionally enable it when result size may exceed memory.

topic: Retries and backoff
detail: Violated: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient connection/server-selection errors and rate-limited responses and cap retries with a dead-lettering approach for permanent failures. Evidence: The sample implements a single short retry for webhook delivery (app/src/worker/watch.js sendWebhook has one retry) but lacks a general exponential-backoff retry strategy for driver transient errors or 429 handling and does not record failed deliveries to a dead-letter store.
proposed_change: Add exponential-backoff retry helper for transient DB and webhook errors and persist failed webhooks to a 'dead-letter' collection after retry exhaustion.

topic: Webhook idempotency
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Make webhook delivery idempotent (include an event id or deduplication key and have the receiver deduplicate), or persist short-lived delivery records so retries don't cause duplicate effects.
proposed_change: A public guidance page stating: 'Include change _id and ruleId in webhook payload and persist delivery attempts to a webhook_deliveries collection for deduplication and observability.'

topic: Mongoose .lean()

proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short 'Driver compatibility' page or section in the DocumentDB quickstart: (1) recommended Node driver major version(s) for each advertised serverVersion; (2) sample package.json snippet showing pinned version and a 'why' paragraph; (3) a brief troubleshooting note explaining common errors when using other driver majors and how to update code for API changes.

topic: .env.example completeness
detail: Missing: .env.example does not enumerate optional pool-tuning environment variables (MAX_POOL_SIZE, MIN_POOL_SIZE, MAX_IDLE_MS) that the code reads/defaults to. Looked in: Repo files (.env.example) and src/db.js; reviewed documentdb-connection skill for recommended knobs. Effect: Users copying .env.example may be unaware of tunable settings in src/db.js and will not know how to adjust pool sizing for their runtime environment.
proposed_change:
[sample_or_quickstart] Add optional entries to .env.example with comments explaining intent, e.g.:
MAX_POOL_SIZE=20 # increase for long-lived servers with high concurrency
MIN_POOL_SIZE=0
MAX_IDLE_MS=300000
Also add a 1-paragraph note in README explaining when to change them.

topic: Server-side aggregation / safe timeline patterns
detail: Missing: A short example page that shows how to implement an index-backed timeline aggregation pipeline with $match/$sort/$group and how to make it safe for large event histories (use allowDiskUse, ranged pagination, cursors). Looked in: documentdb-query-optimizer and aggregation docs; examples exist for $match/$sort but not a compact, sample-friendly 'customer timeline' pipeline plus pagination pattern. Effect: The sample implemented grouping client-side which is unsafe for large timelines; a canonical example would have guided the builder to use a server-side pipeline and pagination from the start.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] A short 'Customer timeline' recipe page: (1) recommended compound index; (2) aggregation pipeline example for timeline + channel grouping; (3) variant for streaming/paged server-side results; (4) note about allowDiskUse and RU impact and a sample explain() showing index usage.

topic: IaC example for DocumentDB clusters
detail: Missing: A minimal Bicep/ARM/Terraform example that provisions Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters (vCore DocumentDB), with defaults for low-cost tiers and clear comments distinguishing it from older databaseAccounts/azurerm_cosmosdb_account examples. Include a README subsection: 'Note: use mongoClusters resource, not databaseAccounts — see link.'

topic: README: clean-up and test guidance
detail: Missing: Explicit clean-up instructions for removing seed data / indexes and guidance on running unit tests without a live cluster (use local DocumentDB gateway image or mock patterns). Looked in: Repo README and documentdb-local-deployment skill; README has setup/run but not teardown or local gateway usage instructions. topic: Tests without live cluster (mocking guidance)
detail: Missing: Concrete guidance or a small helper for writing unit tests that do not require a live DocumentDB cluster (e.g., a lightweight mock of getDb/getClient or a test fixture that starts the local DocumentDB gateway). Looked in: documentdb-local-deployment skill and repository tests; the repo's tests cover only buildPrompt and do not demonstrate mocking DB calls. Effect: Builder added a unit test for the prompt builder only; additional tests for aggregation/seed would require either a live cluster or a documented mocking approach.
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] Provide a test-utils module and README example showing how to stub getDb/getClient with an in-memory collection shim or how to run the DocumentDB local Docker image for integration tests. Include sample jest setup/teardown code.

topic: Server-side aggregation
detail: Violated: In aggregation pipelines, place $match and $sort as early as possible and ensure sort fields are covered by an index (follow ESR: Equality → Sort → Range when designing compound indexes). Evidence: src/aggregationTool.js:8-16 (coll.find({customerId}).sort({timestamp:1}).toArray() then grouping in JS rather than performing the $match/$sort/$group in a single server-side aggregation pipeline).
proposed_change: Replace the client-side grouping with a pipeline like: coll.aggregate([{ $match: { customerId } }, { $sort: { timestamp: 1 } }, { $group: { _id: '$channel', events: { $push: '$$ROOT' } } }], { allowDiskUse: true }).toArray()

topic: Project only required fields
detail: Violated: Project only required fields in find() or aggregation to reduce RU consumption and network transfer (e.g., { timestamp:1, channel:1, eventType:1, metadata:1 }). Evidence: src/aggregationTool.js:8-9 (coll.find({ customerId }).sort({ timestamp: 1 }).toArray() with no projection specified).
proposed_change: Add projection to the find or use a $project stage in the aggregate pipeline: e.g., coll.find({ customerId }, { projection: { timestamp: 1, channel: 1, eventType: 1, metadata: 1 } }).sort({ timestamp: 1 }).toArray()

topic: Retry/backoff on transient errors
detail: Violated: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and explicitly handle 429 (throttling) by honoring Retry-After and retrying after that delay. Evidence: src/db.js:10-17 (clientOptions set retryWrites: true but there is no explicit retry/backoff wrapper for application-level operations or handling of 429/Retry-After).
proposed_change: Add an operation wrapper that retries transient errors with exponential backoff and explicitly handles 429 by reading Retry-After (use a small retry helper or a library like promise-retry).

topic: Avoid unbounded memory
detail: Violated: Avoid unbounded in-memory aggregation ($group that accumulates huge arrays); stream results, page by timestamp ranges, or use $limit and incremental aggregation to keep memory usage bounded. Evidence: src/aggregationTool.js:8-9 (timeline = coll.find(...).sort(...).toArray() loads the whole result set into memory for a customer).
proposed_change: Use a cursor with a reasonable batchSize or implement timestamp-based paging (e.g., timestamp > lastSeen) and stream or paginate results instead of toArray().

topic: Monitoring and RU awareness
detail: Violated: Instrument and monitor RU/s consumption, latency, and throttling for typical aggregations and provision or autoscale throughput so heavy aggregations or vector searches are not routinely throttled. Evidence: No instrumentation for RU/latency/429s is present in application code or README; agent and aggregation code do not record or surface RU metrics.
proposed_change: Add basic diagnostics in the seed/aggregation paths (log duration, catch 429 and surface Retry-After), and document how to enable diagnostic settings in Azure / Log Analytics.

topic: Audit trail: index decision
detail: Violated: Audit trail for key architecture decisions (index choices, driver pinning, auth method). Evidence: events.jsonl:26/21-23 show attempts to call log_decision for provisioning and index decisions that raised validation errors; some design choices (index creation arguments and some run_policy rationale) were attempted to be logged but were not recorded successfully (see events.jsonl entries with 'Invalid arguments for log_decision').
proposed_change: Fix the log_decision invocation to supply a valid reason_source literal (e.g., 'readiness_report' or 'documentdb-indexing') or fallback to a documented CHANGELOG entry in the repo. Ensure each index and major choice is recorded with a decision id.

detail: Cold answer was wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). topic: Q06 Which authentication methods are supported, and how does a driver authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID?
detail: Cold answer was wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). topic: Context-engineering heuristics for DocumentDB RAG
detail: Missing: No documented, service-specific guidance on assembling passages within the LLM token budget (rank by score, distinct timestamps, token-counting examples). topic: Idempotent seed-ingest pattern
detail: Missing: A canonical, idempotent ingestion pattern (bulk upserts or bulk ReplaceOne with upsert=True) and sample code for doing bulk upserts efficiently against DocumentDB. Looked in: Quickstart insert docs and agent-kit skills; no small canonical example for idempotent chunked ingestion was found. detail: Missing: Clear guidance on when and how to enable the DocumentDB MCP management/write tools (ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS / ENABLE_WRITE_TOOLS) that the agent helpers rely on. Looked in: Events and MCP skill docs; the run environment reported management tools are disabled and the error message refers to environment flags but the README doesn't say how to opt in. Example: export ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true'.

topic: Retry/backoff guidance for SDK & embedding calls
detail: Missing: An explicit, service-specific retry/backoff recipe for DocumentDB writes, index builds and embedding-provider calls (include 429 handling and idempotent writes). Looked in: documentdb-connection skill and general docs; no ready-to-copy recipe for sample authors. Effect: No retry/backoff is implemented in sample; transient failures will surface as unhandled exceptions or noisy messages.

detail: Missing: A recommended test scaffold (pytest) and examples that mock MongoDB and embedding models so tests run without a live cluster. Looked in: repo and skill docs. Effect: No tests exist; this makes CI for the sample harder and forces manual verification against a live cluster.

topic: Require TLS
detail: Violated: Require TLS for all connections (connection strings include tls=true) and restrict network access with firewall rules or Private Endpoints. Evidence: src/db.py (lines 12-17) simply passes the URI through to MongoClient; there is no check that tls=true or tls/ssl options are present, nor guidance to enforce Private Endpoint usage in the code.
proposed_change: Validate DOCUMENTDB_URI in get_client() and warn/raise if TLS is not requested (or document that the URI should include tls=true), and add README guidance on network protection.

topic: Least-privilege credentials
detail: Violated: Give application credentials least privilege: create a database-scoped user for the sample app instead of using an admin key or cluster-wide credentials. Evidence: The sample expects a full connection string in DOCUMENTDB_URI (src/db.py line 15). There is no guidance or helper that creates or recommends a DB-scoped user or demonstrates connecting via Microsoft Entra ID/ODIC.
proposed_change: Add README instructions showing how to create a least-privilege database user scoped to sample_fintech_04, or add an example using Microsoft Entra ID OIDC if the cluster supports it.

topic: Conventional indexes for filters
detail: Violated: Also create conventional single-field or compound indexes on frequently filtered fields (e.g., transcript_id, source, chunk_id, start_time). Evidence: src/ingest.py (lines 43-46) creates only a unique index on chunk_id (coll.create_index([('chunk_id',1)], unique=True)). There are no indexes on source or start_time.
proposed_change: Create indexes on 'source' and 'start_time' (or a compound index including transcript/source + start_time) so transcript/time-range filters are efficient.

topic: Use cluster's vector search API
detail: Violated: Run nearest-neighbor queries using the cluster's vector search API (cosmosSearch / $search) with topK and tune search parameters. Evidence: src/query.py (lines 25-40) pulls documents and computes cosine locally; it does not use $search/cosmosSearch aggregation (no server-side vector search call).
proposed_change: When a vector index exists, switch the retrieval path to use $search + cosmosSearch aggregation with topK and $project to fetch only needed fields; keep client-side fallback for local testing.

topic: Metadata pre-filtering
detail: Violated: Apply metadata-based pre-filtering (for example by transcript/source or date range) as part of or before vector search to reduce fan-out and RU/IO costs. Evidence: src/query.py (line 29) only filters on embedding_model in the find call; it does not accept or apply a transcript/source or date-range filter.
proposed_change: Support optional --source or --date-range flags and include them as filters in the aggregation/$search call or in the prefilter find query to reduce candidate set.

topic: Retries and backoff
detail: Violated: Implement exponential backoff and retries for transient network errors and throttling (429), and make writes idempotent so retries don't create duplicates. Evidence: No retry/backoff behavior is present around database writes or embedding calls in src/ingest.py or src/query.py.
proposed_change: Wrap network/DB calls with a retry/backoff wrapper (e.g., tenacity) and ensure upsert semantics for write retries.

topic: Prefer built-in vector search
detail: Violated: Use application-side cosine calculation only as a fallback; prefer built-in vector search APIs for scale and performance. Evidence: src/query.py (lines 25-40) computes cosine similarity in the application over all docs; built-in $search/cosmosSearch is not used.
proposed_change: Add aggregation that calls $search + cosmosSearch when vector index is present; keep client-side scoring for small local datasets.

topic: Sanitize text before embedding
detail: Violated: Sanitize and normalize text before embedding (strip control characters, normalize whitespace, preserve timestamps). Evidence: src/ingest.py (lines 17-35) trims whitespace but does not run control-character sanitization or normalization steps; timestamps are not extracted.
proposed_change: Add a text normalization step before chunking: remove control chars, normalize unicode, collapse whitespace, and extract/preserve inline timestamps; document this in ingest.py and README.

topic: Context-engineering assembly
detail: Violated: Assemble retrieved passages to fit LLM token budget: rank by vector score, concatenate until budget minus answer buffer is reached, prefer distinct timestamps. Evidence: No token-budgeting or timestamp-aware selection exists in src/query.py; the script uses top-k and simple concatenation.
proposed_change: Implement passage selection logic that uses a token estimator (tiktoken or average char→token ratio), reserves an answer buffer, and prefers distinct timestamps if scores are close. Add a README section describing the heuristic.

topic: Create a cosmosSearch vector index (kind vector-ivf, vector-hnsw or vector-diskann) on the embedding field in code, with

topic: Index tuning guidance for samples
detail: Missing: Concise guidance in indexes/README.md and main README explaining how to change lBuild/lSearch/numLists/other vector params for datasets of different sizes and the memory/tier implications. topic: README clean-up instructions

topic: Client timeouts
detail: Violated: Set sensible client timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) and cap query execution with maxTimeMS. Evidence: get_mongo uses MongoClient(uri, retryWrites=False) without explicit serverSelectionTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS (app/search.py:22-27). No per-query maxTimeMS is set on aggregation/find calls (app/search.py:86-116).
proposed_change: Pass sensible timeouts when constructing MongoClient (e.g., MongoClient(uri, retryWrites=False, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, connectTimeoutMS=10000)) and set maxTimeMS on expensive aggregations (e.g., pipeline options or add {maxTimeMS: 120000} to aggregate calls).

topic: Pin dependencies
detail: Violated: The driver version is pinned and is one the service supports (and dependencies are pinned). Evidence: app/requirements.txt lists packages without exact pinned versions (app/requirements.txt).
proposed_change: Pin the packages to tested versions in requirements.txt and include a brief note in README about the tested environment.

topic: Vector index creation
detail: Violated: Create and tune a vector index using the appropriate kind and set tuning parameters and choose the similarity metric. Evidence: indexes/vector_index.json contains an example HNSW config (app/indexes/vector_index.json) but no code applies this index to the live cluster; documentdb_list_indexes returned no such index (events.jsonl).
proposed_change: Add an opt-in index-creation step (script or seed flag) that runs the createIndexes/createSearchIndexes payload using pymongo's db.command or mongosh, guarded as opt-in to avoid accidental production changes.

topic: Projections to exclude embeddings
detail: Violated: Use projections ($project) to return only needed fields and exclude embeddings by default to reduce payload. Evidence: _vector_search fallback fetches embedding fields in-app (app/search.py:120) and the aggregation pipelines project only title/description but the fallback find used to build candidates includes 'embedding' (app/search.py:120). The final fused results returned to the client do not include embedding arrays, but candidate fetches still read embeddings from DB which is acceptable for fallback but not ideal for production.
proposed_change: When fetching candidates for vector similarity, select only product_id and embedding (not full documents) and then project out embedding before returning results; avoid returning embedding in API response.

topic: Seed bulk upsert
detail: Violated: Use bulk write/bulk upsert when ingesting large datasets rather than many single upserts. Evidence: seed/seed.py performs an update_one(upsert=True) per document in a loop (app/seed/seed.py:54-56) instead of using bulkWrite; for 20 docs this is fine but it is not bulk-optimized.
proposed_change: Use collection.bulk_write with UpdateOne operations to upsert documents in batches or use bulkWrite with ordered=False to improve throughput.

topic: Connection timeouts
detail: Violated: Set reasonable connection timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) to fail fast and avoid hung requests, tuned to the application's latency expectations. Evidence: app/src/db.py: MongoClient is created with retryWrites=True but no explicit serverSelectionTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS (line 18).
proposed_change: Set serverSelectionTimeoutMS and sensible connect/socket timeouts when constructing MongoClient (e.g., MongoClient(uri, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, connectTimeoutMS=10000)).

topic: Connection pool tuning
detail: Violated: Configure the MongoClient connection pool (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS) according to the deployment model rather than relying on defaults. Evidence: app/src/db.py: MongoClient created with default pool settings (line 18) and no explicit pool tuning parameters.
proposed_change: Pass tuned pool options for the expected runtime (e.g., maxPoolSize) or read them from env for samples that demonstrate different deployment shapes.

topic: Retryable reads/writes

Evidence: app/src/db.py: MongoClient is created with retryWrites=True (line 18) but the orchestrator and seed do not implement explicit application-level retry/backoff on transient errors.
proposed_change: Wrap critical DB operations (seed, insert_one/update_one) with a small retry helper (exponential backoff) and record idempotency/dedup keys in workflow_runs.

topic: TTL for workflow logs
detail: Violated: Use TTL indexes (expireAfterSeconds on a date field) for ephemeral workflow/log documents so old workflow runs are automatically purged. Evidence: Orchestrator._ensure_indexes creates workflow_runs indexes (lines 78-79) but no TTL index is created to expire workflow documents.
proposed_change: Add a TTL index on a suitable date field (e.g., create an index on {'start_ts':1} with expireAfterSeconds set via create_index or via the DB command) and document retention policy in the README.

topic: Schema versioning

proposed_change: A short public page demonstrating a minimal workflow-run document schema and examples of resuming a run would help agents follow this reliably.

topic: Transactions usage
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Use multi-document transactions only when required for atomicity across documents/collections, keep transactions small and short-lived, and validate transaction behavior against the live cluster.
proposed_change: A documented page stating when DocumentDB supports transactions, plus an integration test recipe that runs against the local DocumentDB gateway or live cluster to validate behavior.

detail: Violated: When running heavy aggregation pipelines, set allowDiskUse=true (or the driver equivalent) and test with explain() so operations that need disk spill are allowed and to avoid memory rejection; use paged or incremental refresh for very large datasets. Evidence: scripts/refresh_summaries.py line 37 calls db.transactions.aggregate(p) with no allowDiskUse argument.
proposed_change: Call aggregate with allowDiskUse=True (db.transactions.aggregate(p, allowDiskUse=True)) and add a note in README to run explain() when scaling.

topic: Explain() and plan inspection
detail: Violated: Use explain("executionStats") and the MCP or diagnostic tools to inspect query and aggregation plans (IXSCAN vs COLLSCAN, keysExamined/docsExamined) and fix COLLSCANs before shipping. Evidence: No explain("executionStats") calls are present in scripts/refresh_summaries.py or seed.py; events show documentdb_list_indexes was used (events.jsonl line 45) but no explain run was recorded.
proposed_change: Add an optional --explain flag to scripts/refresh_summaries.py that runs db.transactions.aggregate(p).explain('executionStats') and prints the plan; include instructions in README to run explain and inspect ixscan/colscan counts.

topic: Retries & idempotency
detail: Violated: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network errors and rate-limiting responses, and prefer idempotent operations when retrying to avoid duplicates. Evidence: app/db.py does not set retry or timeout driver options and the refresh/seed code does not wrap operations in retry/backoff logic.
proposed_change: Set sensible driver-level timeouts and enable retryableWrites/retryableReads where appropriate, and wrap bulk operations with retry/backoff (or use idempotent upserts). Example: MongoClient(MONGO_URI, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, retryWrites=True).

topic: retryableReads/writes & timeouts
detail: Violated: Enable driver retryableReads/retryableWrites when supported and set sensible timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS) so the app fails fast under misconfiguration instead of hanging. Evidence: app/db.py line 18: MongoClient(MONGO_URI) with no explicit retry/timeouts in the code.
proposed_change: Construct MongoClient with appropriate options from env: MongoClient(MONGO_URI, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, connectTimeoutMS=10000, retryWrites=True, retryReads=True).

topic: Top-N query indexes
detail: Violated: Create indexes on fields used for top-N queries or dashboard sorts (or create a compound index matching equality+sort) to avoid in-memory sorts and speed ordered list endpoints. Evidence: No indexes are created on branch_summaries for top-N metrics (e.g., avgTicket or totalVolume). Seed and refresh scripts create indexes only on the transactions collection (scripts/seed.py lines 15-18).
proposed_change: Create indexes on branch_summaries for common sorts/filters; example: db.branch_summaries.create_index([('avgTicket', -1)]) or compound index [('branchId',1), ('avgTicket', -1)] depending on query shapes.

topic: Rate-limit/validate endpoints
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Rate-limit and validate user inputs on expensive endpoints (e.g., refresh and ask); authenticate and authorize refresh operations to avoid accidental large refresh jobs or expensive LLM/vector queries from untrusted callers.
proposed_change: A public page in the docs describing how to protect expensive LLM/refresh endpoints for DocumentDB-backed samples would let an agent add rate-limiting automatically.

topic: Monitoring & diagnostics
detail: Violated: Monitor collection- and cluster-level metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, connections), enable slow-query logging/diagnostics to Log Analytics, and add alerts for sustained saturation or throttling so you can scale or optimize indexes proactively. Evidence: No monitoring, diagnostics or example alerting configuration is present in the repo or README.
proposed_change: Add a README section that instructs users how to enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs, and include an example Log Analytics query and an alert rule for sustained CPU/IO throttling.

topic: Full-text search
detail: Violated: Prefer the DocumentDB search index + $search (createSearchIndexes + $search) and BM25 scoring for full-text search; use fuzzy/phrase settings and custom analyzers rather than the community $text operator. Evidence: The sample uses regex-based lexical retrieval (app/main.py line 38) and does not create or query a createSearchIndexes/$search index.
proposed_change: Add an optional createSearchIndexes example and replace or augment the lexical fallback with a $search-backed retrieval (README should include sample createSearchIndexes payload and $search aggregation example).

topic: A LangChain tool (Python LangChain) takes an analyst's natural-language question and queries the cached summary document
detail: partly_met because tool_unavailable. app/main.py lines 32-49 implement an /ask endpoint that retrieves summaries and composes context; lines 51-66 call OpenAI to produce a natural-language answer. There is no langchain dependency in requirements.txt and decisions.jsonl includes D008 describing removal of langchain due to a pydantic-core native build failure.
proposed_change: Add langchain to requirements and ensure CI/installation uses a pydantic-core wheel or platform where pydantic-core builds succeed (or provide an optional adapter module). Alternatively, supply a small test-only stub in the repo that conforms to LangChain's Tool/Agent interface and document how to swap in real LangChain.

topic: The tool is attached to a LangChain agent or chain so that an analyst can submit a natural-language question (e.g. throu
detail: partly_met because tool_unavailable. app/main.py lines 32-66 show /ask endpoint that composes matched summaries and calls OpenAI chat to return an NL answer (functionally equivalent to a LangChain Tool + agent invocation). No real LangChain agent/chain is present (see decision D008).

topic: Singleton client reuse
detail: Violated: Create a single (singleton) MongoClient/Mongoose connection for the process and tune pool and timeout settings for the deployment type. topic: Prefer Entra ID

topic: Compound index ESR
detail: Violated: Create a compound index that follows ESR (Equality → Sort → Range) so latest-version lookups use assetId then version. Evidence: app/src/models/CollateralAsset.js defines a compound index { assetId: 1, version: -1 } (line 25) and a separate createdAt index (line 26) but not the exact {assetId:1, version:-1, createdAt:-1} compound suggested.
proposed_change: Add a compound index { assetId:1, version:-1, createdAt:-1 } (or ensure the existing indexes are sufficient for the pipeline) to avoid sorts; create it via schema.index or via the seed script's syncIndexes step.

topic: Sparse index for LLM fields
detail: Violated: Use sparse or partial indexes for optional LLM-derived fields (e.g., llmTags.eligibilityTier) to reduce index size and RU costs. Evidence: No partial/sparse index exists for llmTags fields in the model files; only asset/version/createdAt indexes are present (app/src/models/CollateralAsset.js lines 24-30).
proposed_change: Add a partial index such as CollateralAssetSchema.index({ 'llmTags.eligibilityTier': 1 }, { partialFilterExpression: { 'llmTags.eligibilityTier': { $exists: true } } }) to reduce index footprint.

topic: Aggregation pipeline design
detail: Violated: Run server-side aggregation pipelines for summaries and push selective $match/$project stages early (ideally scoped to the partition key). Evidence: app/src/routes/coverage.js builds a pipeline that $sort then $group then $replaceRoot and only after that applies $match for eligibility (lines 17-31). The practice recommends applying $match earlier to reduce scanned docs.
proposed_change: If eligibilityOnly is requested, add a $match stage on llmTags.eligibilityTier BEFORE the $group so the engine can drop non-eligible documents early (or use a two-stage pipeline that materializes latest versions first then filters, depending on index availability).

topic: Retries on throttling
detail: Violated: Implement retries with exponential backoff for throttling (429 / RequestRateTooLarge) and honor service retry headers. Evidence: No application-level retry logic is implemented for database operations; mongoose.connect sets timeouts but writes/aggregations do not implement backoff or honor Retry-After headers (no code in app/src/*).
proposed_change: Add a small retry wrapper for operations that can receive 429 or transient network errors; implement exponential backoff, cap retries, and honor x-ms-retry-after-ms / Retry-After headers when returned by the server.

topic: Embedding metadata
detail: Violated: Normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity and store the embedding model name and dimensions alongside vectors. Evidence: The schema has an optional embedding array and .env.example lists EMBEDDING_DIM, but the code does not normalize embeddings or record embedding model name/dimensions on documents (no code in app/src for normalization or storing model metadata).
proposed_change: If embeddings are used, normalize vectors on write, store { embeddingModel: <name>, embeddingDim: <n> } in the document, and ensure EMBEDDING_DIM in .env.example is documented and used by any index creation script.

topic: Graceful shutdown & pool sizing
detail: Violated: Tune connection pool sizes and concurrent query counts to the cluster limits and close Mongoose connection gracefully on process exit. Evidence: The start() function calls mongoose.connect() but the server lacks a process.on('SIGINT'/'SIGTERM') handler to disconnect gracefully; pool options such as maxPoolSize are not set (app/src/index.js lines 25-32).
proposed_change: Add process signal handlers (SIGINT/SIGTERM) to call mongoose.disconnect() and add configurable pool options to mongoose.connect (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS).

topic: Aggregation push filters early
detail: Violated: When building coverage or aggregate pipelines, push filters and projections early (match → project → group) and scope by partition key to reduce scanned docs. Evidence: Coverage pipeline applies $group/$replaceRoot before applying eligibility $match, which means ineligible docs are processed by grouping/sorting rather than being filtered earlier (app/src/routes/coverage.js lines 17-31).
proposed_change: Reorder the pipeline to $match eligibilityTier (if eligibleOnly) before grouping, or consider a two-stage approach that first finds latest versions and then filters by eligibility with an indexed predicate.

topic: Read preference
detail: Violated: Choose read preference for your distribution; use primaryPreferred for read-after-write consistency in a single primary region. Evidence: The sample does not set readPreference in mongoose.connect; it relies on the client's default. There is no README guidance about read preference choices (app/src/index.js lines 26-32).
proposed_change: Add an optional READ_PREFERENCE or set readPreference: 'primaryPreferred' in mongoose.connect options and document trade-offs in README.

topic: Connection client reuse
detail: Violated: For Python apps prefer one process-global AsyncMongoClient reused across the app lifecycle rather than creating a new Motor AsyncIOMotorClient per request; initialize once and close on shutdown. Evidence: app/src/sample_retail_07/db.py:10-16 creates an AsyncIOMotorClient() inside init_db() on each call and returns db; there is no module-level singleton or get_motor_client implemented (create_indexes.py expects get_motor_client).

topic: Connection pool & timeouts
detail: Violated: Tune Mongo client pool and timeout parameters for the deployment model (serverless: small pools, short maxIdleTimeMS; long-running servers: larger maxPoolSize and longer maxIdleTimeMS) and set serverSelectionTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS to reasonable values for your environment. Evidence: app/src/sample_retail_07/db.py:14 uses AsyncIOMotorClient(uri) without pool or timeout tuning parameters; no serverSelectionTimeoutMS/maxPoolSize set.
proposed_change: Set client options when constructing the client (e.g., AsyncMongoClient(uri, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=20000, maxPoolSize=50) or pass similar Motor options). Prefer a singleton client so pool tuning applies globally.

topic: Indexes for aggregation
detail: Violated: Create indexes to support aggregation/reporting: at minimum index product_id and create a compound index on (product_id, sentiment) when grouping by product and sentiment to accelerate aggregation pipelines. Evidence: src/sample_retail_07/models.py:21-23 declares indexes on product_id and product_id+sentiment_score, but aggregation scripts (app/scripts/aggregate.py:14-16 and src/sample_retail_07/aggregations.py:14-16) group on sentiment_label (different field). The compound index does not include sentiment_label, so the group-by by sentiment_label will not be accelerated.
proposed_change: Change the compound index to (product_id, sentiment_label) or add a separate index on sentiment_label: models.Settings.indexes should include IndexModel([('product_id', ASCENDING), ('sentiment_label', ASCENDING)]).

topic: Application retries
detail: Violated: Implement application retries with exponential backoff for transient errors (network blips, 429 throttling, transient 5xx), and honour Retry-After headers when present. Evidence: No retry/backoff logic is implemented for the OpenAI HTTP call (app/scripts/run_pipeline.py:62-66) or for database writes (app/scripts/run_pipeline.py:92 uses await review.save() with no retries).
proposed_change: Wrap HTTP calls and DB writes in a retry-with-backoff library (tenacity or a small custom loop), detect 429/5xx and honour Retry-After. Implement idempotent retry semantics for upserts.

topic: Retryable writes
detail: Violated: Azure DocumentDB does not support driver-level retryable writes; do not rely on automatic retryable-write semantics—implement safe application-level retries instead. Evidence: No application-level retry logic is present (app/scripts/run_pipeline.py:101-109 and app/scripts/run_pipeline.py:92 save operation). The example .env.example does not explicitly include retryWrites=false; the app may therefore be exposed to write failures without retries.
proposed_change: Do not rely on driver retry semantics. Add app-level retries for upsert/save operations and document in README why this is necessary for Azure DocumentDB (include example code).

topic: Async Python client choice
detail: Violated: Prefer PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient for Python async code (newer async API) rather than Motor; create one AsyncMongoClient and reuse it across the process. topic: Change-stream resume
detail: Violated: Use change streams for real-time alerts and persist resume tokens (resumeAfter / startAtOperationTime) so listeners can recover from restarts; use startAtOperationTime or historical replay when supported to recover older events. Evidence: app/src/main.py lines 87-106 open coll.watch and emit alerts, but do not persist resume tokens or checkpoint progress; scripts/demo_change_stream.py uses a short-lived watch to demo the event (no durable resume).
proposed_change: Durably persist resume tokens (e.g., to a small checkpoints collection) periodically and use resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime on startup; smallest code change: write lastChange['_id'] or returned resume token to a checkpoints collection and pass resumeAfter on watch.

topic: Retry semantics
detail: Violated: Azure DocumentDB often recommends setting retryWrites=false in connection strings for compatibility; drivers should still use retryable reads where supported and application-level retries should be idempotent with exponential backoff for transient errors and throttling (429). Evidence: app/src/db.py normalized_uri enforces retryWrites=false (lines 24-29) but the application does not implement idempotent application-level retries (inserts use doc.insert() and insert_many without retry wrappers).
proposed_change: Implement idempotent application-level retries with exponential backoff around writes (and make operations idempotent where needed). Smallest fix: add a retry helper that catches transient errors (e.g., network/timeouts/429) and retries with backoff and idempotency tokens.

topic: Change-stream checkpointing
detail: Violated: When running change-stream listeners, checkpoint progress (durably store resume tokens) and keep one watcher per resume token (one thread/process per physical partition) to avoid losing events on crashes. Evidence: app/src/main.py change_stream_monitor (lines 87-106) opens a watch and prints alerts but does not store resume tokens or checkpoint to durable storage; demo_change_stream.py uses a short-lived watch for demo only.
proposed_change: Persist resume tokens to a durable collection and resume with resumeAfter on restart; implement one watcher per physical shard token for scale.

proposed_change: Wrap DB calls in a small retry helper (e.g., using tenacity) or enable and document pymongo retry options; add a simple retry decorator for key DB operations (aggregation, update_one) with exponential backoff and honoring Retry-After where applicable.

topic: JSON Schema validation

topic: Projection and RU cost
detail: Violated: Use explain and query metrics to shape queries so they return only needed fields and avoid scanning large fields; project/limit fields to reduce network bandwidth and RU costs where possible. Evidence: The agents fetch full documents (criteriaDocs = await criteriaColl.find(...).toArray()) and preauth is retrieved with findOne({ _id }) returning full doc; there is no projection to exclude large fields.
proposed_change: Project only necessary fields in queries (e.g., criteriaColl.find({ procedureCode: ... }, { projection: { procedureCode: 1, severityTags: 1, criteriaText: 1 } })) to minimize bandwidth and RU consumption.

topic: Collection-level JSON Schema
detail: Violated: If you need JSON Schema enforcement, use the service's $jsonSchema / schema-validation features to declare required fields and types at collection creation or with validation rules. Evidence: No validator rules defined in seed.js during collection creation.
proposed_change: Add JSON Schema validators for preauth_requests and submissions in seed.js (db.createCollection with validator) to enforce presence and types of key fields.

topic: PHI in logs
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Do not log PHI or sensitive patient data and redact or exclude identifying fields from diagnostics and logs; ensure log retention and access meet compliance requirements.
proposed_change: A short official guidance page stating recommended fields to redact (patientId, clinician, clinicalNotes) and example code for redaction and secure log handling.

topic: Persist intermediate state
detail: Violated: Persist intermediate orchestrator state (reviewResult, letterDraft) so orchestrator logic is resumable and idempotent, allowing retries without duplication. Evidence: Orchestrator does not persist intermediate reviewResult or letter draft; it only writes final submission and status updates (app/src/orchestrator.js lines 26-35).
proposed_change: Persist review result and draft as fields on the preauth document (e.g., reviewResult, draftDocument, reviewAt) using upsert so orchestrator can resume after interruptions.

topic: Concurrent update controls
detail: prior_knowledge_only: When updating shuffled/competing documents concurrently use optimistic concurrency (version) or a conditional findOneAndUpdate with version-check to avoid lost updates; the service itself does not mandate a single pattern so implement per-app.
proposed_change: A short guidance page showing the recommended optimistic-concurrency pattern for DocumentDB's MongoDB-compatible API.

topic: Precompute maturity bucket
detail: Violated: If you compute maturity buckets frequently, store a precomputed maturity_bucket field at write time (denormalize) or otherwise ensure the fields used for bucket/group are indexed to avoid full-collection scans at query time. Evidence: src/aggregation_tool.py:30-36 computes maturity_years at query time using $addFields instead of using a stored maturity_bucket; seed.py does not write a maturity_bucket field.
proposed_change: Change seed.py to compute and upsert a 'maturity_bucket' field per document (stable bucket labels) or add a migration script that backfills the field; use that stored field as the group key in the aggregation pipeline.

topic: Early filtering in pipelines
detail: Violated: Place selective $match stages as early as possible in aggregation pipelines and project only required fields to minimize data scanned and RU/IO consumption. Evidence: src/aggregation_tool.py pipeline does not include an early $match to reduce scanned documents before $bucket; pipeline starts with $addFields computing maturity_years (lines 30-37).
proposed_change: If the sample will be used on larger datasets, add an optional date-range or currency $match before $addFields, or precompute maturity_bucket and $match on that field.

topic: Use explain() to validate aggregation
detail: Violated: Validate and tune aggregation pipelines with explain('executionStats') to confirm index usage and avoid COLLSCAN before running production workloads. Evidence: No call to explain() or MCP explain tool is present in the repository; aggregation_tool.py runs the pipeline directly (src/aggregation_tool.py:72).
proposed_change: Add a developer command or script to run coll.aggregate(pipeline).explain('executionStats') (or use the documentdb MCP explain tool) and surface index-use warnings in CI/local checks.

topic: Retry handling
detail: Violated: Implement retry handling for transient errors with exponential backoff and jitter, limit retries, and treat non-idempotent writes specially. Evidence: src/seed.py and src/aggregation_tool.py perform DB operations without explicit retry wrappers; get_client uses serverSelectionTimeoutMS but no retry/backoff logic is present.
proposed_change: Wrap network operations (seed bulk_write, aggregate) with a retry/backoff helper that handles pymongo network exceptions; or use built-in driver retryWrites where appropriate and document behavior for non-idempotent writes.

topic: Limit aggregation results
detail: Violated: Avoid returning unbounded aggregation results: use $limit, pagination, server-side cursors, and reasonable batchSize. Evidence: src/aggregation_tool.py converts the full aggregation cursor into a list (results = list(coll.aggregate(pipeline))). No $limit or server-side cursor iteration is used.
proposed_change: Iterate the aggregation cursor (do not materialize list) and/or add $limit/pagination to the pipeline; in CLI examples, keep results small or stream output.

topic: JSON Schema validators
detail: Violated: Use collection-level JSON Schema validators ($jsonSchema) to enforce required fields and types at insert/update. Evidence: No collection validator creation is present; seed.py upserts documents but does not create a validator on the positions collection.
proposed_change: Add a migration/seed step that ensures a $jsonSchema validator for the positions collection enforcing maturity_date, rate_type, notional and coupon_rate types.

topic: Idempotent index creation
detail: Violated: Make index creation idempotent and keep index creation in migration/seed scripts rather than creating indexes ad-hoc at runtime. Evidence: Index creation is done in aggregation_tool._ensure_index() (src/aggregation_tool.py:14-16) at query-time rather than in a migration/seed step; although create_index is idempotent, best practice is to put index lifecycle in seeds/migrations.
proposed_change: Move create_index calls into seed.py (or a dedicated migrations script) and check existing indexes before creating new ones.

topic: Retries for transient errors
detail: Violated: Implement retry logic for transient errors and 429 rate-limits with exponential backoff and honor Retry-After when provided. Evidence: Code uses MongoClient with retryWrites: true (src/client.js line 14) but there is no application-level retry/backoff wrapper for transient network errors or 429s around DB operations (seed/generate do not implement retries).
proposed_change: Add an exponential-backoff retry wrapper for DB operations and honor any Retry-After headers returned by the service (or use a supported library wrapper).

topic: Create indexes before seeding
detail: Violated: Create required indexes before seeding or significant reads, and verify indexes at deployment time (listIndexes/listIndexes check) in your provisioning/seed scripts. Evidence: src/seed.js performs replaceOne/upsert for segments (line 29-31) and then creates indexes after those writes (lines 33-35). The recommended order is to create indexes before bulk seeding to avoid write amplification or unintended write costs.
proposed_change: Create indexes (createIndex) before running upserts/loads, and add a verification step that lists indexes and ensures they exist. Update src/seed.js to createIndex prior to replaceOne.

topic: WriteConcern/readPreference
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Design writeConcern and readPreference intentionally for cross-replica durability or latency needs, but verify Azure DocumentDB's default mapping and supported features first.
proposed_change: A single doc in the product docs that states the supported writeConcern levels, default mapping and sample driver options for Node.js.

topic: Idempotent writes / upsert
detail: Violated: Make writes idempotent or use upsert (e.g., replaceOne / updateOne with upsert: true) so retries do not create duplicates. Evidence: src/seed.js uses upsert replaceOne (line 30) for segments, but src/generate.js inserts campaigns with campaigns.insertOne(doc) (line 85) which can create duplicates on retries.
proposed_change: Use updateOne/replaceOne with an idempotency key or upsert for campaign writes (e.g. include a stable dedupe key or use updateOne({ segmentId, someUniqueKey }, { $set: doc }, { upsert: true })).

topic: Explain & slow-query logging

topic: Projection for prompt building
