topic: Retries & idempotent retries
detail: Violated: Enable driver retryable reads/writes where supported and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff for idempotent operations. Evidence: app/src/db.js line 15 sets retryWrites: true, but the app does not implement application-level retry/backoff for idempotent operations (no retry wrapper around send or DB operations).
proposed_change: Add an application-level retry wrapper (exponential backoff) for idempotent DB ops and for read retries; ensure non-idempotent side effects (sends) are guarded by idempotency checks before retrying.

topic: Change-stream resume tokens
detail: Violated: Persist change-stream resume tokens to durable storage and resume streams using resumeAfter or startAtOperationTime. Evidence: app/src/listener.js opens coll.watch() (line 10) but does not persist resume tokens or call watch() with resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime on startup.
proposed_change: Persist the change._id (resume token) after processing each change (or periodically) into a durable collection (e.g., consumer_checkpoints) and on startup pass resumeAfter with the last token to coll.watch().

topic: Change-stream error handling
detail: Violated: Handle change-stream errors explicitly: persist resume progress frequently, attempt resumes for resumable/transient errors, and provide a safe recovery plan for non-resumable errors. Evidence: app/src/listener.js registers change handler but has no handlers for changeStream.on('error') or logic to attempt resume/reopen; only SIGINT shutdown is implemented (lines 25-30).
proposed_change: Add error event handlers that decide resumable vs non-resumable based on error codes, attempt resume/reconnect with backoff for transient errors, and escalate or replay a bounded window for non-resumable errors.

topic: Projection for queries
detail: Violated: Use projection to return only the fields needed for a query to reduce network transfer and RU/IO consumption. Evidence: app/src/orchestrator.js line 9 uses customers.findOne({ customerId: event.customerId }) without projection; server.js returns full outreach_logs documents (app/src/server.js lines 7-10).
proposed_change: Use projection in customers.findOne() to request only the fields needed by the copy agent (e.g., name, preferred_channel, profile) and modify /logs to exclude sensitive or large fields unless explicitly requested.

topic: TTL index for outreach logs
detail: Violated: For temporary or retention-based logs use a TTL index on a timestamp field to automatically expire old records. Evidence: Seed script creates outreach_logs.eventId index but no TTL index on sentAt (app/src/seed.js lines 32-36).
proposed_change: Create a TTL index e.g. db.collection('outreach_logs').createIndex({ sentAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 60 * 60 * 24 * 30 }) and document retention policy in README.

topic: Idempotency for external side effects
detail: Violated: Implement idempotency for external side effects (e.g., sending outreach): store and check an idempotency key such as event id or outreach_id to avoid duplicate sends on replay. Evidence: The sendAgent writes outreach_logs after composing a record but does not check for pre-existing outreach_logs.eventId before sending; no unique constraint on eventId is enforced in seed.
proposed_change: Add an idempotency check in orchestrator or sendAgent: ensure outreach_logs has a unique index on eventId and check/skip sends when a record exists; or insert with upsert semantics and only perform external side-effects on successful insert.

topic: Resume token persistence vs writeConcern
detail: Violated: Persist change-stream consumer progress durably but do not rely on client-side writeConcern: Azure DocumentDB handles quorum for writes and client writeConcern may be ignored. Evidence: No resume token persistence is implemented (app/src/listener.js). The code does not configure any client-side writeConcern for checkpoint writes to a durable collection.
proposed_change: Persist resume tokens to a durable collection and on startup resume from the last token; do not rely on setting writeConcern:majority in the client since the service documents that client writeConcern may be ignored.

topic: Backpressure & batching
detail: Violated: Avoid unbounded aggregations or map-reduce in change-stream consumers; process events in bounded batches, apply backpressure, and limit concurrency. Evidence: listener.js invokes orchestrator.processEvent for each change directly with no concurrency/batching/limiting logic (app/src/listener.js lines 11-19).
proposed_change: Add a bounded worker queue or semaphore throttle around processEvent and consider batching updates for non-latency-critical work; implement backpressure for sustained high-throughput streams.

topic: PII logging
detail: Violated: Do not log full PII or credentials; redact or avoid persisting sensitive customer attributes in logs or persisted traces. Evidence: app/src/sendAgent.js line 22 logs the full record in sandbox mode; outreach_logs stores the full message and does not redact PII (app/src/sendAgent.js lines 11-20).
proposed_change: Redact PII in console logs and consider storing only customerId and a message hash or store a redacted message in outreach_logs; document PII retention policy in README.

topic: Idempotent writes / upsert
detail: Violated: Use upsert operations and idempotent update patterns (or transactions where supported) for write-heavy merge/upsert workflows to avoid duplicate or inconsistent golden records on retries. Evidence: app/src/agents.py: write_golden performs insert (lines 124-127 and lines 129-135) and does not use upsert/replace semantics or a merge-operation id to make the operation idempotent.
proposed_change: Use an upsert (replaceOne with upsert: true) keyed by a deterministic merge-id or check for an existing golden record marker before inserting, or use a unique constraint and handle duplicate-key errors to make merges idempotent.

topic: Retry/backoff
detail: Violated: Implement exponential backoff with jitter for transient faults and retries, and only retry idempotent operations (or make non-idempotent workflows safe to retry). Evidence: app code does not implement client-side retry/backoff logic; network/operation calls use default driver behavior (no explicit retry wrapper).
proposed_change: Add a small retry wrapper for idempotent operations (or rely on driver's documented retry plus respect retry-after headers). For non-idempotent merges, add merge-status tracking to allow safe retries.

topic: TLS enforcement
detail: Violated: Always connect with TLS (tls=true / TLS enabled) and do not disable certificate validation in production so traffic to the cluster is encrypted. Evidence: app/src/db.js uses the URI supplied in DOCUMENTDB_URI and does not enforce TLS in mongoose.connect options (app/src/db.js lines 15-23). app/.env.example shows an example URI that includes tls=true (app/.env.example line 2) but code does not validate/enforce it.
proposed_change: Validate the provided connection string contains tls=true (or set tls: true in mongoose.connect options) and fail early with an explanatory error when TLS appears disabled.

topic: Connection tuning
detail: Violated: Tune driver connection options to your environment (pool sizing, timeouts and maxIdleTimeMS) and pick different sensible defaults for serverless vs long-running processes. Evidence: app/src/db.js comments reference sensible defaults but the connect call does not set pool sizing or timeout options (app/src/db.js lines 17-23).
proposed_change: Read pool and timeout settings from environment (e.g., MAX_POOL_SIZE, SERVER_SELECTION_TIMEOUT_MS, SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS) and pass them into mongoose.connect; document recommended defaults for sample vs production.

topic: Retry/backoff
detail: Violated: Enable driver retryable reads/writes where supported and implement application-level exponential backoff + jitter (and respect Retry-After / retry-after-ms headers) for throttling and transient faults. Evidence: app/src/db.js sets retryWrites: true (line 21) but bulkWrite usage in app/src/worker.js catches errors without inspecting writeErrors, retrying idempotent ops, or honoring Retry-After headers (lines 64-69 and 75-80).
proposed_change: On bulkWrite failures inspect error/writeErrors, treat duplicate-key (11000) as expected for idempotency, and implement retries with exponential backoff + jitter for transient errors/429 responses, respecting Retry-After when provided.

topic: Cursor batch size
detail: Violated: For large scans use server-side cursors/getMore with a controlled batchSize (cursor + batchSize) instead of fetching all documents at once. Evidence: Worker uses Account.find(filter).cursor() (app/src/worker.js line 44) and BATCH_SIZE for write batching (line 9) but does not set cursor.batchSize(BATCH_SIZE) or otherwise control server-side batchSize.
proposed_change: Use Account.find(filter).select(...).lean().batchSize(BATCH_SIZE).cursor() to control server-side getMore batchSize and reduce memory/RU spikes.

topic: Projection and lean()
detail: Violated: Apply projection (return only fields needed) and, in Mongoose, prefer lean() when you don't need full Mongoose documents to reduce memory and driver overhead. Evidence: Worker reads full account documents via Account.find(filter).cursor() without .select(...) or .lean() (app/src/worker.js line 44).
proposed_change: Change the cursor to Account.find(filter).select('balance interestRate _id').lean().batchSize(BATCH_SIZE).cursor() to reduce memory and Mongoose overhead.

topic: Create indexes idempotently
detail: Violated: Create indexes idempotently at deployment/migration time and verify index existence before running large scans to avoid runtime index builds during high-load jobs. Evidence: Indexes are created by the worker at run time via ensureIndexes() (app/src/worker.js lines 12-31). That causes index creation to happen when the job runs rather than at deployment/migration time.
proposed_change: Provide a separate idempotent migration script (or include index creation in seed/migrate step run at deploy time) and have the worker verify index existence but not trigger heavy background builds at job runtime.

topic: Monitor RUs and 429s
detail: Violated: Monitor request charge (RUs), RU/s utilization and 429 counts (throttling), enable diagnostic/slow-query logging, and alert on saturation so you can scale or reduce batch sizes before jobs fail. Evidence: No code instruments requestCharge, 429 counts, or logs slow queries; worker simply runs queries and prints summary (no monitoring integration).
proposed_change: Log requestCharge (if returned), add counters for 429s and total request charge, and document recommended alerts; optionally expose a --dry-run or --profile flag that runs queries with explain('executionStats') and logs keysExamined/docsExamined.

topic: Bulk write partial failures
detail: Violated: Treat bulkWrite partial failures as an expected outcome: inspect results and writeErrors, retry only idempotent operations, and suppress/handle duplicate-key (11000) errors when using unique constraints for idempotency. Evidence: Worker catches bulkWrite exceptions but does not inspect writeErrors nor retry idempotent operations or specially handle duplicate-key (11000) errors (app/src/worker.js lines 64-69 and 75-80).
proposed_change: Inspect bulkWrite response for writeErrors; treat duplicate-key 11000 as expected and move on; implement retries with backoff for transient failures and log non-idempotent failures for human review.

proposed_change: Call await ApiCache.createIndexes() in src/seed.js or at the application startup before inserting seed data, and log results so index creation is explicit in the sample.

Looked in: documentdb-vector-search skill and vector search docs. Effect: Seed script uses conservative defaults appropriate for demo; users may not know how to adapt them for larger datasets, risking poor recall or excessive build time if copied unchanged.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] An 'Index tuning' section in README: explain m/efConstruction semantics, suggested presets for demo/10k/100k+ vectors, how to change DIMS and algorithm in seed.py, and an example of how to run a small recall vs latency experiment.

topic: Retry/backoff and honoring Retry-After
detail: Missing: The public quickstarts and sample did not include a small retry utility or example showing how to honor Retry-After (x-ms-retry-after-ms) for both DocumentDB queries and external embedding APIs. Looked in: Optimize throughput and Retry-After docs; events show no retry implementation in code. Effect: Sample has no retry/backoff; a user copying the sample into production may experience 429 throttling and unbounded retries or poor resilience.
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] Add a small retry helper in the agent-kit: a decorator that implements exponential backoff with jitter and reads Retry-After/x-ms-retry-after-ms headers; include example usage around seed/createIndexes and around embedding provider calls.

topic: Projection to exclude embeddings
detail: Missing: Quickstart sample code examples often demonstrate returning entire documents which include embeddings; the best-practice of projecting out embedding vectors before returning results is not prominent. Looked in: documentdb-vector-search skill and sample code. Effect: The sample's API response schema excludes embedding, but the aggregation pipeline still retrieves and transports the embedding from the server, causing unnecessary RU and bandwidth cost.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] Add a short note and code snippet to the vector-search quickstart showing $project usage that excludes the embedding field (e.g., { $project: { score: { $meta: 'searchScore' }, name: 1, specialty: 1, languages: 1, insurance: 1 } }).

topic: Embedding metadata (model & dims)
detail: Missing: No explicit demonstration of storing embeddingModel/embeddingDims metadata with documents in the quickstart sample, making it harder to track model drift. Looked in: documentdb-vector-search guidance and agent-kit resources. Effect: Sample uses a consistent embedding size but does not record metadata per-document; future reindexing or drift detection would be harder.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Add a one-paragraph recommendation in the vector-search quickstart and a code snippet: store embeddingModel, embeddingDims and embeddingVersion fields in each document at ingest time.

topic: Local guidance for LlamaIndex/OpenAI installs
detail: Missing: Pip dependency resolution pitfalls for llama-index/openai combinations are common; the sample's README mentions optional LlamaIndex but there is no tested extras/install recipe that guarantees compatibility. Looked in: events.jsonl shows repeated pip resolver failures when attempting to install llama-index; agent attempted several version pins. Effect: Builder removed llama-index from runtime to make the sample runnable. Users following the README might still fail to install llama-index if versions are not specified precisely.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Provide an explicit 'Optional: install LlamaIndex and OpenAI' section in README that pins a tested set of versions (e.g., llama-index==0.14.26, openai==1.8.0) and includes a virtualenv/constraints file and a note about incompatibilities with older Python versions; include a small 'tox' or CI job that verifies the extras install.

topic: Missing IaC sample for mongoClusters
detail: Missing: The sample lacks a Bicep/Terraform example showing how to create an Azure DocumentDB mongoClusters resource; quickstarts confuse databaseAccounts vs mongoClusters in other docs. Looked in: readiness_findings and template docs (learn.microsoft.com) indicate Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters is the correct resource type. Effect: No IaC was included; teams copying the sample may attempt to use the wrong resource type and fail to provision cluster properties needed for vector search.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] Add a minimal Bicep file (or Terraform) that creates Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameters (sku, region, storage) and a short note: 'Use this only with approval — the demo uses an existing cluster.'

topic: Public guidance on multi-document transactions (prior_knowledge_only)
detail: Missing: The public docs do not state a clear recommendation about avoiding multi-document transactions for vector-search read-heavy paths (the agent's prior knowledge came from other MongoDB practices). Looked in: search for transaction guidance and change-stream docs; discovered_practices flagged K22 as prior_knowledge_only. Effect: The sample does not use transactions; however, builders relying on MongoDB memory might either overuse transactions or avoid them unnecessarily. Agents have no authoritative guidance to rely on.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short FAQ entry: when to use multi-document transactions in Azure DocumentDB, trade-offs for read-heavy vector-search workloads, and example code recommending single-document upserts for ripple-safe ingest.

topic: Retry on transient errors
detail: Violated: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient errors and explicitly honor throttling responses (HTTP 429) by reading the service-provided retry header (e.g., x-ms-retry-after-ms / Retry-After) before retrying. Evidence: app/app/db.py and app/seed.py show no retry/backoff implementation (app/app/db.py:14-23; seed.py:62-67 prints exception but does not retry).
proposed_change: Add a retry wrapper for DB operations with exponential backoff, jitter, and respect for Retry-After headers; implement retries around embedding/remote calls too.

topic: Pre-filter before vector search
detail: Violated: Use structured filters inside the cosmosSearch operator (the 'filter' field) to narrow candidates (e.g., specialty, language, insurance) before vector similarity search rather than post-filtering after kNN. Evidence: app/app/main.py constructs a $search aggregation with only a vector clause (app/app/main.py:62-71) and does not include a 'filter' clause for structured fields.
proposed_change: Add optional structured filtering to /find-provider (e.g., parse 'Spanish' / 'Medicare' out of the query or accept filter parameters) and include them in the cosmosSearch.filter clause so the kNN is run on a narrowed candidate set.

topic: Indexes for filters
detail: Violated: Create Mongo-style single-field or compound indexes on fields used in equality or range filters (e.g., specialty, languages, acceptedInsurance) and prefer compound indexes (ESR: Equality→Sort→Range) when queries combine fields. Evidence: seed.py ensure_index creates only the vector index (seed.py:52-61) and does not create indexes for specialty, languages or insurance.
proposed_change: Create single-field indexes on specialty, languages and acceptedInsurance (or a compound index if queries commonly combine them) in ensure_index; document index write-cost tradeoffs in README.

topic: Project out embeddings
detail: Violated: When returning API responses, project out (exclude) the embedding vector and return only the metadata fields and the similarity score to reduce network and client processing costs. Evidence: The aggregation pipeline in app/app/main.py (lines 62-75) projects $$ROOT into 'doc' so that the embedding is retrieved; while the API response omits embedding by schema, the DB still returns embedding, increasing RU and bandwidth.
proposed_change: Change the $project stage to exclude the embedding field (e.g., project only the fields needed and score) so the DB does not return large embedding arrays.

topic: Back off on 429s
detail: Violated: Respect platform rate-limiting: back off on 429s, avoid tight retry loops, add jitter to retry delays, and limit retry attempts to prevent thundering-herd effects. Evidence: No code detects or respects 429/Retry-After headers in DB operations or embedding calls; seed.py catches createIndexes exceptions but does not honor Retry-After (seed.py:62-67).
proposed_change: Add retry/backoff logic that reads Retry-After/x-ms-retry-after-ms headers and implements exponential backoff with jitter; limit attempts to a safe maximum.

topic: Transactions guidance
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Avoid multi-document transactions for common read-heavy vector-search paths; prefer single-document atomic operations and optimistic concurrency where possible.
proposed_change: A short guidance page stating whether the avoidance of multi-document transactions (common in MongoDB guidance) applies specifically to Azure DocumentDB for vector-search workloads, and when to prefer single-document upserts vs transactions.

topic: Normalize searchable text fields
detail: Violated: Normalize searchable text fields (lowercase, canonicalized language tags) at ingest so equality/index lookups and language matching are reliable. Evidence: seed.py upserts fields as provided by data/providers.json (seed.py:75-81) and does not normalize language tags or canonicalize fields for filters.
proposed_change: Normalize language tags and other filterable metadata at ingest (lowercase, canonical tags); e.g., add doc['languages_normalized'] and store languages as lowercase ISO codes.

topic: Build the service in Python with LlamaIndex, and use LlamaIndex to produce the embedding vectors stored with the provide
detail: not_met because tool_unavailable. README.md (lines 6-8), app/seed.py (lines 30-43) — code uses OpenAI (when available) or a deterministic fallback embedding generator; llama-index is not installed or used.
proposed_change: Add llama-index and a compatible openai pin to requirements.txt (or add an extras install target), and update seed.py and app/main.py to call LlamaIndex's embedding pipeline when available; include a CI step that installs those packages to surface dependency issues early.

topic: Embed the incoming request with LlamaIndex and run the similarity search inside Azure DocumentDB with a $search / cosmos
detail: partly_met because tool_unavailable. app/app/main.py (lines 42-57) embeds request with OpenAI (when available) or a deterministic fallback and then runs an aggregation pipeline with $search/cosmosSearch (lines 62-71). LlamaIndex is not used.
proposed_change: Either add LlamaIndex to the runtime (requirements) and use its embedding adapter in main.py/seed.py, or update README to state explicitly that LlamaIndex is optional and show the minimal code changes to enable it (preferred: add a small helper that delegates to LlamaIndex when installed).

topic: Q01 What is the Azure resource provider namespace and resource type of an Azure DocumentDB cluster?
detail: Cold answer was wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). Build risk: If the builder attempted to deploy or reference Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts (instead of Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters) they would be targeting the RU-based Cosmos DB account resource; ARM/Bicep/Terraform templates and CLI calls would be incorrect for vCore clusters and the builder might fail to find or create the intended resource.
proposed_change: Update quickstart and sample templates to use Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters for vCore clusters and explicitly note the distinction from Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts (the RU Cosmos DB account). | Add a short deprecation/clarification note on the top of any docs that still show databaseAccounts for MongoDB use to point readers to mongoClusters when they intend vCore clusters.

topic: Q02 Which Azure CLI command group creates and manages a cluster? Is it in the core CLI or an extension?
detail: Cold answer was partly_wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). Build risk: Using az cosmosdb create (databaseAccounts) would create or target the RU-based Cosmos DB account resource and not the vCore mongoClusters; the wrong CLI group will lead to provisioning/management failures for the intended cluster type.
proposed_change: Clarify in the Azure CLI quickstarts and samples the exact command group to use for vCore DocumentDB clusters (az documentdb mongocluster or az cosmosdb mongocluster) and call out whether the command is in a preview/extension. | Add a note in the 'az cosmosdb' docs that points to 'az documentdb' commands for vCore workloads so agents don't conflate the two.

topic: Q03 Which Bicep and Terraform resource types deploy a cluster?
detail: Cold answer was wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). Build risk: Using the databaseAccounts/azurerm_cosmosdb_account resource type will not create the intended vCore mongo cluster; deployment templates would target the wrong product and fail validation or produce a mismatched resource.
proposed_change: Update sample IaC templates and the agent kit templates to use Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters for vCore clusters and include one-liner guidance that azurerm_cosmosdb_account is for RU-based Cosmos accounts.

topic: Q04 What does a connection string look like: scheme, host suffix, port, and the options it must carry?
detail: Cold answer was partly_wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). Build risk: Using the Cosmos (10255) connection-string pattern against a vCore DocumentDB cluster may fail to connect or misuse required auth/query options; the sample must read the provided DOCUMENTDB_URI (per run environment) and pass it unchanged to mongoose/MongoClient.
proposed_change: In all Node/README samples, instruct builders to read DOCUMENTDB_URI from env and not to hard-code connection string patterns; show both common patterns (10255/cosmos-host and mongoClusters SRV) and explain which one applies.

topic: Q05 How is capacity provisioned and billed: request units, compute tiers with vCores, serverless, or something else?
detail: Cold answer was wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). Build risk: If the builder assumed RU-based pricing/throughput they might attempt to set RU throughput parameters in code or IaC for a vCore cluster and fail to configure or size the cluster correctly.
proposed_change: Add an explicit statement in the quickstarts and agent kit that vCore DocumentDB clusters use compute (vCore) SKUs (e.g., M30) and are not provisioned via RU/s. | Add a short comparison table (vCore vs RU) to the 'getting started' doc for agents to consult.

topic: Q06 Which authentication methods are supported, and how does a driver authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID?
detail: Cold answer was partly_wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). Build risk: If the builder attempts to implement Entra auth by passing an OAuth token as a normal password with authSource='$external' they will use the wrong auth mechanism and connections will fail. Use the documented MONGODB-OIDC connection-string parameters or the portal-provided connection strings.
proposed_change: Document the precise connection-string parameters and example code snippets for common driver platforms (Node.js, mongosh, MongoDB Compass) that show MONGODB-OIDC usage and managed-identity examples.

topic: Q08 Which vector index types are supported, and what does the command that creates one look like?
detail: Cold answer was wrong (confused with mongodb_atlas_or_server). Build risk: If the builder used the Atlas-style createIndex call, index creation would fail. Use the documentdb createIndexes templates (cosmosSearch/cosmosSearchOptions) documented in the vector-search docs.
proposed_change: Provide a short 'create vector index' code snippet for Node.js in the agent kit and quickstarts using createIndexes + cosmosSearchOptions to reduce copying of Atlas syntax.

topic: Q09 How are full-text search and hybrid search done?
detail: Cold answer was partly_wrong (confused with open_source_documentdb). Build risk: If the builder wired in Azure Cognitive Search rather than using createSearchIndexes they would add unnecessary infrastructure and complexity and miss the native hybrid search primitives documented for DocumentDB.
proposed_change: Document the recommended route (createSearchIndexes + $search + RRF) clearly in the agent-kit search guidance and discourage routine use of external search services unless there's a specific reason.

topic: Q10 Which MongoDB wire protocol or server versions are supported, and which commonly used MongoDB features are not?
detail: Cold answer was partly_wrong (confused with mongodb_atlas_or_server). Build risk: Assuming a certain server-version feature (for example a stage introduced in a later MongoDB release) without verifying the cluster’s serverVersion could cause runtime errors.
proposed_change: Encourage samples to read the cluster's serverVersion (via portal/az or the documentdb MCP server) and confirm required operators against the compatibility matrix before using them.

topic: Q11 How do you run the database locally for development and tests: which image or emulator, and which port?
detail: Cold answer was wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). Build risk: Trying to run the Cosmos DB emulator (or expecting 10255) instead of the DocumentDB gateway (10260) will make the local dev instance not match the intended cluster configuration; the sample run-environment requires using the live cluster but the local gateway instructions in the skill should be followed if the builder chooses to run a local container.
proposed_change: Add an explicit 'local dev vs emulator' note to the quickstart README that states: use the DocumentDB gateway image (port 10260) for DocumentDB vCore local parity and the Cosmos DB emulator only for Cosmos (RU) accounts.

topic: Q12 Are change streams supported, and does anything have to be enabled first?
detail: Cold answer was partly_wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). Build risk: If the builder assumes multi-shard change streams are on by default they may attempt to open a cluster-wide stream and fail; check cluster Features and enable multi-shard change streams if the sample intends to exercise that capability.
proposed_change: Add a confirmation step in the sample README: ‘If you need multi-shard change streams enable the cluster feature: Features > Change streams for multishard clusters’ and link to the portal steps.

topic: Q14 What was this service called before, and how does it relate to Azure Cosmos DB and to the open-source DocumentDB pro
detail: Cold answer was partly_wrong (confused with legacy_vcore_naming). Build risk: Public-facing sample text that uses the wrong product name may mislead users; CLI and template commands may target the wrong resource type if the wrong name is used.
proposed_change: Add an explicit 'naming and mapping' FAQ page in the agent kit that maps 'Azure DocumentDB', 'Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore)', and 'Azure Cosmos DB (RU)' to their resource types and intended use-cases.

topic: Q15 What engine is underneath, and does that change anything in application code?
detail: Cold answer was wrong (confused with azure_cosmos_db_for_mongodb_ru). Build risk: If the builder assumes a Cosmos DB RU engine they might reach for RU-specific features or configuration and run into incompatible behavior.
proposed_change: State the engine explicitly in the agent kit landing page and in sample READMEs: 'Azure DocumentDB runs on DocumentDB (open-source) and supports MongoDB drivers; compare to Cosmos (RU) where noted.'

topic: API surface choices for /nearby endpoint
detail: The prompt did not specify whether /nearby should accept lat/lon/radius as query parameters or JSON body, nor naming conventions (lat/lng or lat/lon) or error-handling behaviors. I checked the prompt review and docs; this is an API design choice and not specified by any skill or Learn page. The builder must pick a convention (recommend: query params ?lat=&lon=&radiusMeters=) and document it in README.
proposed_change: Document this where the agent looked.

topic: Seed dataset content and licensing
detail: The prompt leaves unspecified what sample dataset to include (size, realistic coordinates, stock model). Documentdb-local-deployment skill shows how to seed data but does not supply a canonical example dataset or license. The builder should create a small synthetic idempotent seed (10–20 stores) and include it in the repo; the decision isn't answered by any skill.
proposed_change: Document this where the agent looked.

topic: Definition of done / acceptance tests
detail: No single authoritative source states exact acceptance criteria for this sample (number of returned results, sorting tolerances, edge cases). The builder must choose reasonable criteria (e.g., /nearby returns stores sorted by distance, distance includes returned distance field in meters, opens/closes filter works) and document test steps.
proposed_change: Document this where the agent looked.

topic: DocumentDB Agent Kit (npx skills add Azure/documentdb-agent-kit) - would bundle example repos and quickstart scaffolding
detail: Exists and would have sped this build up, but was not installed.
proposed_change: Mention it in the kit's setup skill, or make the pipeline install it.

topic: mongosh
detail: Useful for interactive debugging and ad-hoc verification of collections/indexes; install mongosh (MongoDB Shell) on the dev machine or use Docker client images. Workaround: the documentdb MCP server provides equivalent data-plane commands (documentdb_find_documents, documentdb_aggregate, documentdb_list_indexes, documentdb_explain_operation) that the agent should use if mongosh is absent.
proposed_change: Useful for interactive debugging and ad-hoc verification of collections/indexes; install mongosh (MongoDB Shell) on the dev machine or use Docker client images. Workaround: the documentdb MCP server provides equivalent data-plane commands (documentdb_find_documents, documentdb_aggregate, documentdb_list_indexes, documentdb_explain_operation) that the agent should use if mongosh is absent.

topic: Mongoose autoIndex production guidance
detail: Missing: No Azure-DocumentDB-specific public guidance on whether Mongoose autoIndex should be disabled in production (the discovery returned prior knowledge only). Looked in: Searched installed skills and web for 'Mongoose autoIndex Azure DocumentDB' and repository search (events.jsonl search_text). Effect: Builder did not disable autoIndex explicitly; seed script creates indexes but there is no explicit production configuration to disable autoIndex. Agents relying on memory may not disable autoIndex when they should.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] A short 'Mongoose on Azure DocumentDB' doc: state that autoIndex should be disabled in production (autoIndex:false) and show the recommended pattern (create indexes in migration/seed scripts) with a code snippet and example env-based toggle. Include a 1-paragraph rationale and example Bicep/az CLI migration step.

topic: Lat/lon & radius validation guidance
detail: Missing: No public DocumentDB-specific guidance found during discovery on validating latitude/longitude ranges and enforcing max radius for geo endpoints. Looked in: Searched skills and web: 'validate lat lon input azure documentdb', 'sanitize geospatial query radius best practice'. Effect: The /nearby endpoint only checks numeric params (NaN) and does not clamp/reject out-of-range coordinates or limit max radius, leaving API vulnerable to expensive or abusive queries unless the developer adds safeguards.
proposed_change: [learn_doc] Add a short paragraph to the Geo queries page advising: validate lat ∈ [-90,90], lon ∈ [-180,180], enforce a default maximum radius (e.g., 50km), and include code snippets for server-side validation and returning 400 on invalid input.

topic: Driver version pinning discoverability
detail: Missing: Agent did not surface the official guidance about tested Mongoose/MongoDB driver versions by discovery; it was found only by name search. The quickstart docs do list tested driver versions. Looked in: learn.microsoft.com quickstart and tutorial pages for Mongoose + Azure DocumentDB (found by targeted search). Effect: Builder used caret ranges in package.json but package-lock.json pinned versions for the build. Agents following default choices might not pick a driver version that the docs explicitly tested.
proposed_change: [discoverability] Make the 'Tested driver versions' and 'Recommended Mongoose/driver pairing' more visible on the quickstart/tutorial landing page; add one-line 'Tested with Mongoose X.Y.Z (MongoDB driver A.B.C)' near the top so agents find it by general search.

topic: Retry & transient error guidance
detail: Missing: Samples and quickstarts mention connection options but a concise example of application-level retries (exponential backoff + honoring Retry-After) for the Node.js/Mongoose stack on DocumentDB was not prominent. Looked in: documentdb-connection skill and quickstart pages; discovery located general guidance but not a compact Node.js example. Effect: No retry logic was added to the sample; transient failures and HTTP 429s are not handled specifically by the API, increasing risk in real deployments.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] A short 'Retries and backoff' example in the documentdb-connection skill: Node.js snippet showing a small retry wrapper (with exponential backoff) for DB operations and handling 429 with Retry-After. Include guidance when driver-level retries are sufficient vs when app-level retries are required.

topic: README clean-up and test guidance
detail: Missing: README did not include explicit cleanup steps nor guidance for running tests without a live cluster. Looked in: Repository README and quickstart; no cleanup or test instructions found. Effect: Users receiving the sample may not know how to remove the created sample data or run tests offline; it increases friction for CI and local experimentation.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] Add a 'Clean-up' section showing how to drop the stores collection (mongo shell or node snippet) and an optional 'Testing' section that shows how to run unit tests with mongodb-memory-server or mocks and what environment variables are required.

topic: IaC example using mongoClusters
detail: Missing: No example IaC template (Bicep/Terraform) showing Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource for vCore clusters was included. Looked in: Repo and quickstart IaC; none in sample. Readiness findings noted agent confusion between databaseAccounts and mongoClusters. Effect: Operators who try to supply infrastructure-as-code may target the wrong resource type (databaseAccounts) or leave out tier/storage parameters; this increases risk of incorrect provisioning.
proposed_change: [sample_or_quickstart] Provide a minimal Bicep template that creates Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameterized sku/tier and region, plus sample az CLI commands; add a short note clarifying difference from Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts (RU-based Cosmos).

topic: MCP management tool opt-in note
detail: Missing: The MCP 'create_index' tool failed in this run with an opt-in requirement (ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS). There was no repo-level note about MCP opt-in settings. Looked in: events.jsonl (tool error) and repository (no mention). Effect: Builder attempted to use MCP create_index and the tool failed; they fell back to seed.createIndexes. Future builders/agents will retry the MCP tool unless informed about opt-in.
proposed_change: [agent_kit_rule] A short agent-kit rule or README note: 'When using MCP management tools in this environment you may need to set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true; otherwise fall back to application-level index creation.'

topic: Least-privilege credentials
detail: Violated: Use least-privilege credentials for application access (prefer Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC or per-app users with minimal roles rather than cluster admin/root credentials). Evidence: The sample reads DOCUMENTDB_URI without guidance on least-privilege credentials; neither README nor seed scripts create a limited user account or state that the provided string should be least-privileged.
proposed_change: Add README guidance and an example for creating/using a least-privilege DB user or Microsoft Entra ID authentication. Include a short shell/az command or mongo shell snippet showing how to create a per-app user.

topic: Connection timeouts
detail: Violated: Set sensible connection and socket timeouts and configure the connection pool (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, socketTimeoutMS, serverSelectionTimeoutMS). Evidence: app/src/index.js uses mongoose.connect(URI, { dbName: 'sample_retail_20' }) with no explicit pool or timeout options; no socketTimeoutMS or serverSelectionTimeoutMS are set in code.
proposed_change: Pass sensible connection options from env (e.g., { maxPoolSize: parseInt(process.env.DB_MAX_POOL||'10'), socketTimeoutMS: 30000, serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 5000 }) or document recommended defaults in README and the documentdb-connection skill.

topic: Pagination
detail: Violated: Use pagination (limit + skip or range-based cursors) for large result sets and avoid unbounded queries to prevent resource overconsumption and huge responses. Evidence: app/src/routes/nearby.js runs aggregation without limit or pagination (no limit/skip or cursor usage; line 36 returns all results).
proposed_change: Add limit and optional page/cursor parameters to /nearby (e.g., ?limit=50&after=<cursor> or ?page=1&limit=25). If returning large lists, use a cursor-based approach to avoid skip for large offsets.

topic: Retries
detail: Violated: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors and on rate-limited responses (HTTP 429), and honor Retry-After headers when provided. Evidence: No retry-with-backoff logic is present in repository; seed/verify and /nearby handler do not implement explicit retry behaviour.
proposed_change: Implement an application-level retry wrapper for transient errors and honor 429 Retry-After; or use driver-retry settings when appropriate. Add a small retry helper and use it around critical DB operations (with bounded attempts and exponential backoff).

topic: Mongoose autoIndex
detail: prior_knowledge_only: When using Mongoose in production, avoid enabling autoIndex; prefer controlled index builds as part of deployment.
proposed_change: A sentence in a 'Mongoose on Azure DocumentDB' page stating: 'Disable autoIndex in production (autoIndex:false) and create indexes explicitly during deployment.'

topic: Input validation
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Validate and sanitize latitude/longitude input ranges (lat between -90 and 90, lon between -180 and 180) and enforce a reasonable maximum radius for geospatial queries to prevent abusive or expensive queries.
proposed_change: An authoritative short paragraph on the Geo queries page: 'Validate lat ∈ [-90,90], lon ∈ [-180,180], and clamp or reject radii above X meters (default X=50km)'.

topic: Index naming
detail: Violated: Give indexes meaningful names and include index definitions in deployment manifests or migration scripts so operators can reconcile indexes created by the app versus ops tooling. Evidence: Schema index is defined but no explicit index name or deployment manifest is provided; created index appears as default name location_2dsphere (events.jsonl documentdb_list_indexes output).
proposed_change: Include an index-creation script or deployment manifest that names the index explicitly and add it to repo (e.g., createIndexes command with name and options).

topic: Log pipeline & explain
detail: Violated: Log aggregation pipelines and explain() output in non-sensitive debugging logs when diagnosing query performance, but avoid logging connection strings, credentials, or other secrets. Evidence: No logging of aggregation pipeline or explain() output in repo; morgan is enabled (app/src/index.js line 8) but no debug logging of aggregation/explain output is present.
proposed_change: Add an optional verbose debug mode (controlled by env var) that logs the pipeline and, when enabled, runs explain('executionStats') and logs the result to non-sensitive logs.

topic: Entra ID recommendation
detail: Violated: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID with RBAC and customer-managed keys (CMK) for production clusters with compliance requirements rather than only long-lived passwords or default service-managed keys. Evidence: README and sample code do not document or demonstrate Microsoft Entra ID authentication or explain why password-mode is used for the sample. The code accepts DOCUMENTDB_URI but doesn't show Entra ID usage examples.
proposed_change: Add a README section explaining Entra ID vs password authentication, and provide an example or link for using MONGODB-OIDC/Microsoft Entra ID for production clusters.

topic: Q03 Which Bicep and Terraform resource types deploy a cluster?
detail: Cold answer was partly_wrong (confused with unknown). Build risk: Bicep or AzAPI deployment would target an undocumented API version. Not central if the builder uses an existing cluster.
proposed_change: The model retained a resource schema date but dropped its preview suffix. This is API-version fabrication, not evidence of choosing another database service.

topic: Q08 Which vector index types are supported, and what does the command that creates one look like?
detail: Cold answer was partly_wrong (confused with unknown). Build risk: Oversized clustering can impair small-catalog retrieval or index construction; searching one list does not guarantee the global top 10.

topic: Grounded recommendation explanations
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Ground explanations in retrieved attributes/counts/session preferences and validate returned IDs against ranked candidates.
proposed_change: An agent-output rule with fixed candidate membership, trusted-field merging, explanation evidence references and tests for fabricated purchases/preferences.

topic: Index drift readiness checks
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Use idempotent setup comparing existing index definitions and verify vector readiness before recommendations.
proposed_change: A vector setup rule with normalized definition comparison, drift errors, bounded readiness probing and explicit permission requirements.

topic: Embedding lifecycle metadata
detail: prior_knowledge_only: Persist model identity/version and source-content hash, regenerating embeddings when source content or model changes.
proposed_change: An embedding lifecycle page specifying source hashes, provider/model revision identifiers, normalization versions, cache invalidation and deliberate index rebuilds.

topic: Measured DiskANN search tuning
detail: Violated: Keep k <= lSearch and tune lSearch within 10–1000 against measured recall and latency. Evidence: app/src/repository.js:50 correctly uses k=30/lSearch=40, but app/README.md:127 and the execution trace provide no measured tuning.
proposed_change: Retain the legal defaults for the demo, add a representative recall/latency benchmark, and document how to adjust lSearch while maintaining k <= lSearch.

topic: Measured DiskANN build tuning
detail: Violated: Tune maxDegree and lBuild on representative data rather than assuming defaults meet accuracy/build-cost requirements. Evidence: app/src/repository.js:8 uses 32/50; app/README.md:9 states the values without measurements or scaling instructions.
proposed_change: Label these as unbenchmarked teaching defaults and add a tuning procedure measuring recall, build time and resource usage on representative catalogs.

topic: Vector eligibility prefiltering
detail: Violated: When filtering vector candidates, place eligibility predicates inside cosmosSearch.filter and index the filtered properties. Evidence: app/src/repository.js:50,82 applies anchor and metadata exclusions after ANN retrieval. The deliberate overfetch makes this defensible for the tiny homogeneous catalog, but it differs from public prefilter guidance.
proposed_change: Push anchor eligibility into cosmosSearch.filter using the existing _id index. If supporting mixed-model catalogs, prefilter model metadata with the corresponding standard indexes rather than filtering after top-k.

topic: Decision persistence integrity
detail: Violated: Persist distinct decision records without losing previously logged choices. Evidence: events.jsonl:83-92 returns 'Recorded as D002' for ten distinct choices; decisions.jsonl retains only D002 and D002b. events.jsonl:100-101 then records logger exceptions. Index/auth/model choices were logged in events, not silently made.
proposed_change: Fix unique-ID allocation and atomic append/validation in log_decision; recover distinct event-backed decisions with provenance rather than attributing the loss to the builder.

topic: Unlogged package registry choice
detail: Violated: Record environment-specific package-registry choices that affect sample reproducibility. Evidence: app/package-lock.json:22,36,47,60 pins tarball URLs to the runner's ms-feed-25.pkgs.visualstudio.com feed; no decision explains public portability of this registry choice.
proposed_change: Document and verify anonymous clean-machine access to the pinned feed, or regenerate and review the lockfile using the intended public registry. Log the publishing choice.

topic: Dependency security verification
detail: listed_not_found: Resolve or explicitly assess reported dependency vulnerabilities before publication.
proposed_change: A gallery security gate and an available dependency-audit tool returning advisory details, affected paths, compatible remediation options and exceptions.

topic: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
detail: partly_met because skill_silent. app/.env.example:3-4 lists both environment inputs. Database, models, dimensions, and embedding version remain fixed settings in app/src/config.js:3-9 rather than appearing in that inventory.
proposed_change: Add a sample-packaging rule: inventory every setting, distinguish fixed defaults from configurable environment inputs, and include placeholders for every required input.

topic: The vector index parameters are chosen for the catalog size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
detail: partly_met because skill_silent. app/src/catalog.js:11-22 defines 60 products; app/src/repository.js:7-8,50 uses default-like DiskANN values. app/README.md:7-10 states values but gives no larger-catalog tuning procedure or measurements.
proposed_change: Extend the vector skill with a gallery rule requiring a README tuning section: catalog vector count, default rationale, representative recall/latency measurements, and where to change maxDegree, lBuild, k, and lSearch.
